items.title: Spring UserReport [2026.07.04] Externally launched spring crashed with code 0
Generate SVG examples in CI and automatically commit updates to pull request branches
items.body:
## Goal

Allow contributors to push source changes without repeatedly building Planorama and regenerating SVGs locally. GitHub Actions should generate the complete set of maintained example/snapshot SVGs and, when they change, **automatically append an SVG-only commit to the same pull request branch**.

The normal same-repository PR flow should not require downloading a patch or manually committing generated images.

## Current behavior

Verified against main at [9822017](https://github.com/ritz-p/planorama/commit/9822017192268d8efe15a2480eb9883a36ee5bf9).

- [scripts/update-examples.sh](https://github.com/ritz-p/planorama/blob/9822017192268d8efe15a2480eb9883a36ee5bf9/scripts/update-examples.sh) builds the CLI and regenerates the JSON-based examples in the environment running the script.
- Two maintained SVG snapshots are updated separately through opt-in test paths:
  - `examples/hierarchy-routing.svg`: `UPDATE_ROUTING_SNAPSHOT=1`, `hierarchy_obstacles_and_direct_container_endpoints` in [tests/unit/layout/containers.rs](https://github.com/ritz-p/planorama/blob/9822017192268d8efe15a2480eb9883a36ee5bf9/tests/unit/layout/containers.rs).
  - `examples/port-collisions.svg`: `UPDATE_PORT_SNAPSHOT=1`, `refined_flat_bundle_keeps_opposite_role_port` in [tests/unit/layout/ports.rs](https://github.com/ritz-p/planorama/blob/9822017192268d8efe15a2480eb9883a36ee5bf9/tests/unit/layout/ports.rs).
- These separate update paths required follow-up snapshot updates during #324 and #325.
- The existing workflows validate changes but do not generate and commit updated SVGs. [Tests](https://github.com/ritz-p/planorama/blob/9822017192268d8efe15a2480eb9883a36ee5bf9/.github/workflows/cargo_test.yml) and the other existing validation workflows already support `workflow_dispatch`.

## Proposed behavior

1. On relevant PR updates, or a manual retry, capture the source PR head SHA and generate from that exact revision.
2. Run one canonical generation entry point covering all maintained example SVGs, **including both snapshots above**, large examples, and multi-state/cross-state examples.
3. After generation succeeds completely, check whether any declared generated SVG outputs changed.
4. For a writable same-repository PR, confirm the branch still points to the captured source SHA, then append a bot commit containing only those SVG updates to that branch.
5. Run the applicable validation workflows for the updated PR and confirm their results correspond to the updated commit.

A no-diff run should succeed without making a commit. Generation must be able to run before existing SVG comparison tests pass: source-only changes may legitimately make those comparisons fail until regeneration completes.

## Generation contract

- Share the local and CI generation entry point or output manifest, so new fixtures do not silently escape CI regeneration.
- Reuse the existing snapshot fixture builders rather than maintaining duplicate fixtures or renderer implementations. Do not require the entire test suite merely to generate the two additional snapshots.
- Use the repository's pinned Rust toolchain, locked dependencies, and committed fixtures. Generation must not require live Terraform infrastructure or cloud credentials.
- Explicitly allowlist generated SVG outputs. Do not automatically commit source code, JSON fixtures, documentation, or original icon assets.
- Keep generation deterministic. A second run on the resulting commit must produce no changes.
- Do not commit partial output if any generation step fails.
- Include the changed file list, source SHA, and generated commit SHA in the workflow summary. Provide downloadable complete output/patch artifacts when automatic writeback is unavailable.

## Writeback and CI integration

- Enable automatic commits for same-repository PRs; give only the necessary writeback/dispatch jobs the required `contents: write` / `actions: write` permissions.
- Use normal fast-forward updates, never force-push. If the source branch advances while generation runs, discard the stale result and retry against the newer revision.
- Make the flow idempotent and prevent bot-triggered loops. Do not rely solely on PR path filters: the overall PR diff still contains the original source changes after an SVG-only commit.
- Coordinate concurrent runs per PR without leaving a successfully pushed generated commit unvalidated.
- Prefer `GITHUB_TOKEN` plus explicit `workflow_dispatch` of the applicable existing checks, subject to validating the repository's required-check behavior. GitHub suppresses ordinary push-triggered runs from `GITHUB_TOKEN`; related PR-triggered runs can require approval. Do not assume a bot push automatically completes all checks.
- Dispatch uses a branch/tag ref, which may advance. Track the resulting run and verify its `head_sha`; never report an older or different commit's success as validation of the generated commit.
- Preserve the applicable formatting, Clippy, test, and MSRV coverage, including the existing PR/base merge validation semantics where required. Ordinary PR checkout and branch-based dispatch do not inherently test the same revision.
- If the standard-token approach cannot satisfy required checks without manual intervention, document the alternative using a narrowly scoped GitHub App installation token and its necessary setup.
- For fork PRs or branches where writeback is disallowed, return a usable SVG patch/artifact and document the fallback. Do not execute untrusted PR code with elevated `pull_request_target` permissions to bypass this restriction.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A renderer/source-only change in a same-repository PR automatically receives the necessary SVG updates as a commit on that same PR branch.
- [ ] Both `hierarchy-routing.svg` and `port-collisions.svg` are included in the canonical generation flow.
- [ ] Unchanged output and repeated execution create no commits or endless workflow runs.
- [ ] The new generated commit receives the applicable required checks; this is verified in a real PR rather than inferred from checks on the previous head.
- [ ] A concurrent human push cannot be overwritten or receive stale generated output; dispatch races cannot misattribute validation results.
- [ ] Failed generation produces no partial automatic commit.
- [ ] Fork/read-only cases provide a usable patch/artifact without requiring elevated execution of PR code.
- [ ] Documentation explains the local command, CI flow, generated output scope, permissions, and fallback behavior.

## Related work and references

- #250: CI concurrency; coordinate cancellation/writeback behavior.
- #252: test workflow splitting; avoid duplicating expensive generation unnecessarily.
- #324, #325: recent example and snapshot updates that motivated this workflow.
- [GitHub: triggering workflows and GITHUB_TOKEN behavior](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/trigger-a-workflow)
- [GitHub: workflow dispatch API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflows#create-a-workflow-dispatch-event)

Research: migrate OSA Alias to React/Next.js + TypeScript on Cloudflare Workers
items.body:
## Summary

OSA Alias is not a web app. It is a roughly 500-line Go HTTP/HTTPS server that:

- looks up `_redirect.<host>` TXT records;
- issues redirects;
- gets Let's Encrypt certificates on demand for any hostname pointed at it (`autocert`, binding :80 and :443).

The redirect logic is easy to port to a Worker in TypeScript (S). The hard part is TLS. Workers cannot terminate TLS for arbitrary unknown hostnames on demand. On Cloudflare the equivalent is **Cloudflare for SaaS custom hostnames**, where each hostname must be registered through the API before Cloudflare accepts its traffic. That breaks today's "no accounts, no dashboard" model and adds a small onboarding UI.

Next.js is only relevant for that onboarding UI and the docs page. The redirect engine should be a plain Worker. The realistic scope is:

- a TS Worker port of the engine;
- an optional small Next.js app for hostname registration;
- keeping the Go server as the self-host edition.

## Current architecture

- **Size:** 28 tracked files, 1147 lines of Go including tests.
  - Source: `server.go` 238 lines, `parse.go` 41, `translate.go` 65, `blocklist.go` 33.
  - Tests: `*_test.go` including `e2e_test.go` and `integration_test.go`.
- **Language and dependencies:** Go 1.25 (`go.mod`), using `golang.org/x/crypto` (`acme/autocert`) and `golang.org/x/net` (`publicsuffix`).
- **Request flow** (`server.go`):
  - `redirectHandler` checks the blocklist and calls `net.LookupTXT("_redirect." + host)`.
  - `getRedirect` tries path rules before catch-all rules (`parse.go` regexes, `translate.go` wildcard substitution).
  - It answers with `http.Redirect`, adding `Cache-Control: max-age=86400` for 301/308. Anything unresolved goes to `FALLBACK_URL` with the reason in the fragment.
- **TLS:** `autocert.Manager`.
  - `HostPolicy` only issues certificates when a valid TXT rule exists.
  - `rateLimitedCache` caps issuance at 2 certificates per apex per week. The counter is in memory and resets on restart.
  - Certificates are stored on disk in `CERT_DIR`, a DigitalOcean volume.
- **Configuration:** env vars `BLOCKLIST` (apex list), `FALLBACK_URL`, `PORT` and `CERT_DIR`.
- **Ops:**
  - `Dockerfile` (scratch image);
  - `redirect-name.service` (systemd, `CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE`);
  - `terraform/` (DigitalOcean droplet plus cert volume);
  - `docs/index.html`, a static docs site via GitHub Pages `CNAME`.
- **Not present:** database, auth, UI, jobs.

## Target architecture

- **`alias-worker`:** a TypeScript Worker (Hono or a plain `fetch` handler) on the Cloudflare for SaaS fallback origin. On each request it:
  1. reads `request.headers.get('host')`;
  2. checks the blocklist (KV);
  3. resolves TXT through DNS-over-HTTPS (`fetch('https://cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query?name=_redirect.<host>&type=TXT', { headers: { accept: 'application/dns-json' } })`), or through `node:dns` under `nodejs_compat` if it supports `resolveTxt` (to verify);
  4. caches the parsed rules in KV or the Cache API with a short TTL;
  5. redirects.
- **Custom hostnames:** each user hostname is a Cloudflare for SaaS custom hostname on an OSA zone. Cloudflare issues and renews certificates (HTTP DCV once the CNAME points at us).
- **`alias-web` (optional):** Next.js App Router + shadcn on OpenNext, with docs and a "register my hostname" form. The flow:
  1. check the `_redirect` TXT and the CNAME;
  2. call the custom hostnames API;
  3. store the hostname and its status in D1;
  4. poll the hostname status from a Cron Trigger.
- **D1** (`alias-db`) for registered hostnames, status and abuse flags. **KV** for the blocklist and the rule cache.

## Component mapping

| Current component | Target on Cloudflare | Notes / risk |
|---|---|---|
| `parse.go`, `translate.go` (rules engine) | TS module in the Worker | Direct port. Port the Go tests as Vitest fixtures to guarantee identical behaviour. Go `regexp` and JS `RegExp` semantics are close for these patterns (to verify the wildcard `ReplaceAllString` behaviour). |
| `net.LookupTXT` | DoH `fetch` to 1.1.1.1, or `node:dns` | Adds a subrequest per uncached request. Cache the rules. |
| `autocert` on-demand TLS (:80/:443) | Cloudflare for SaaS custom hostnames | **Biggest change.** Hostnames must be pre-registered via API. Unknown hostnames are rejected at the Cloudflare edge before reaching the Worker (to verify the exact behaviour). Pricing: a free allowance, then a per-hostname monthly fee (to verify the current numbers). |
| A record to a fixed IP (`45.55.126.223`) for apex domains | CNAME flattening at the user's DNS provider, or Cloudflare "apex proxying" | Apex proxying with dedicated IPs is an Enterprise feature (to verify). Users without CNAME flattening would lose apex support. |
| `rateLimitedCache` (Let's Encrypt limits) | Not needed | Cloudflare manages issuance. Instead, limit registrations per user/IP with the rate-limiting binding. |
| `BLOCKLIST` env | KV (or D1) list, editable without redeploy | |
| `FALLBACK_URL` | Worker var | |
| `/healthz` | Worker route | |
| `docs/index.html` (GitHub Pages) | Static page in `alias-web`, or Workers static assets | |
| Docker, systemd, Terraform (DigitalOcean) | wrangler; Terraform `cloudflare` provider (optional) | Keep the Go deployment as the self-host option. |

## Blockers and limits on Workers

- **Workers cannot bind :80/:443 or run an ACME client** for arbitrary hostnames. On-demand TLS as it works today is impossible on Workers. The only path is Cloudflare for SaaS.
- **The product model changes:** "point DNS and it just works" becomes "point DNS, then register once" (via form or API). An auto-registration trick is not possible, because the request never reaches the Worker until the hostname is registered (to verify).
- **Cost scales with users:** custom hostnames beyond the free allowance are billed per hostname.
- **Apex domains:** the fixed-IP A-record path does not translate directly.
- **CPU, memory and subrequests:** trivial for this workload. Not a concern.
- **Cloudflare Containers** could run the Go binary unchanged, but inbound traffic still enters through a Worker and Cloudflare's TLS. So it does not solve on-demand TLS for foreign hostnames (to verify), and it adds no value over the Worker port.

**Verdict:** a full migration is viable only by accepting the Cloudflare for SaaS registration model. Keeping the Go server as the canonical self-host edition is recommended either way.

## Upstream-sync impact

- Upstream redirect.name is active (Dependabot bumps, docs changes).
- A TS Worker is a separate implementation: it cannot merge upstream Go changes, but the rule syntax and test fixtures can be kept in sync manually.
- Suggested layout:
  - keep this repo synced with upstream as is (Go);
  - put the Worker edition in a subfolder (for example `worker/`) or a new repo, and treat `parse_test.go` and `translate_test.go` as the shared conformance suite.

## License note

redirect.name is MIT. Porting the logic to TS is allowed as long as the copyright and license notice is kept in the ported files or the `LICENSE`.

## Phased plan

| Phase | Scope | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Decision: Worker edition yes/no, and standalone vs merged with OSA Short custom domains. Spec in `docs/specs/`. | S |
| 1 | TS port of parse, translate and blocklist, with Vitest fixtures ported from the Go tests. | S |
| 2 | Worker: DoH resolution, rule cache in KV/Cache API, fallback, healthz, deploy with wrangler. | S |
| 3 | Cloudflare for SaaS setup: OSA zone, fallback origin, custom hostname API client, D1 table, Cron status poller. | M |
| 4 | `alias-web`: Next.js docs page + registration form + status page (shadcn, OpenNext). | M |
| 5 | Abuse controls: registration rate limits, blocklist admin, reporting. | S |

Total: **M**.

## Open questions

- Is the per-hostname cost of Cloudflare for SaaS acceptable for a free public service?
- Do we keep apex support for users without CNAME flattening? If yes, how?
- Should registration require an account (and therefore OSA identity), or stay anonymous with TXT-based proof of control?
- Do we merge this into OSA Short's custom-domain feature instead of keeping two apps?
- Should OSA also accept the Forward Domain TXT syntax?

## Checklist

- [ ] Confirm the Cloudflare for SaaS behaviour for unregistered hostnames, plus its pricing and limits
- [ ] Confirm the apex options (CNAME flattening vs apex proxying)
- [ ] Spike: TS rules engine passing the ported Go test fixtures
- [ ] Spike: DoH TXT lookup with caching in a Worker
- [ ] Decide standalone vs merged with OSA Short
- [ ] Spec `docs/specs/001-workers-edition/` (spec, plan, tasks) if approved

items.title: [P1] Spring 6.2.20商用修正とBoot 3.5サポート継続・移行方針を決定する
items.body:
Parent: #86 / #8

Issue #80のOSV基準ではGHSA-j9f9-w8pj-32f8（CVE-2026-47890、SSE view fragments）とGHSA-pc63-qcmh-9cmg（CVE-2026-47884、XsltView）がCRITICALとして検出されています。現REST sourceで利用条件に一致する機能は見つからず、productionの外部設定は未検証です。無期限受容やOSV抑制はしません。

公式修正版はSpring Framework6.2.20ですがEnterprise Support Onlyです。公開修正版7.0.9への移行はBoot4/Framework7の互換性評価を要し、今回の依存patch PRでmajorを変更しません。Boot3.5.16は2026-06-25の最終OSS releaseで、継続OSSサポートがあるとは扱いません。

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] 2026-10-14までに責任者と商用6.2.20取得可否、または独立したBoot4移行計画を決定する。
- [ ] 2026-10-26までに修正を適用しJava17/全回帰/実CI/OSVを検証する。未達の場合は理由・新期限・責任者を記録して再承認する。
- [ ] SSEとXsltViewの実利用/外部設定を確認し、条件が確認された場合は独立緊急是正として48時間以内の対策へ昇格する。
- [ ] OSV CRITICAL分類と、ベンダーLOW（SSE）/MEDIUM（XsltView）評価を区別し、findingを無条件に消さない。
- [ ] 商用artifactへのアクセスは正規license/認証を確認し、scanner/CIへproduction secretを渡さない。

公式根拠:
- https://spring.io/security/cve-2026-47890/
- https://spring.io/security/cve-2026-47884/
- https://spring.io/blog/2026/06/25/spring-boot-3-5-16-available-now/

main直接push/自己merge、AWS・本番DB・既存Docker volume操作、Deploy有効化は禁止。

items.title: Manage the Cloudflare tunnels and their DNS records in iac/app
items.body:
#269 moved the `cloudflared` containers to `iac/app`, but each environment's tunnel, its ingress config and its DNS record are still in `iac/server`. That leaves two things to keep in sync by hand:

- The ingress ports (`http://localhost:8080` / `8081`) in `cloudflare_zero_trust_tunnel_cloudflared_config` have to match `local.environments.*.port` in `iac/app`. Changing a port takes a hand apply of `iac/server` timed with a deploy.
- The tunnel token goes from a data source in `iac/server`, to the `DEV_TUNNEL_TOKEN` / `PROD_TUNNEL_TOKEN` GitHub Actions secrets, to `TF_VAR_tunnel_token`, to the container.

Moving them to `iac/app` lets each workspace own its whole path from hostname to container. Adding an environment then mostly means one more entry in `local.environments`. The cost is a Cloudflare API token in CI, which #269 ruled out. This issue proposes a scoped one.

## Design

- **What moves, per environment:** `cloudflare_zero_trust_tunnel_cloudflared`, `cloudflare_zero_trust_tunnel_cloudflared_config`, the `cloudflare_zero_trust_tunnel_cloudflared_token` data source and the `cloudflare_dns_record` (`dev.doedensonline.nl` for dev, `doedensonline.nl` for prod). The zone, its settings, the `www` record, the redirect ruleset and the SES records stay in `iac/server`.
- **Scoped deploy token.** `iac/server` creates a `cloudflare_account_token` with Cloudflare Tunnel Write on the account, and DNS Write and Zone Read on the `doedensonline.nl` zone. It publishes the token as one `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` secret, without the `DEV_`/`PROD_` prefix: tunnel permissions only scope to the whole account, and both hostnames are in one zone, so per-environment tokens wouldn't be narrower. The provider reads the token from the environment, like the AWS credentials, so `iac/app` gets no new variable.
- **No account or zone ID variables.** `iac/app` looks up the zone with `data "cloudflare_zone"` (filtered on the domain) and takes the account ID from `data.cloudflare_zone.this.account.id`. This is also what makes the import blocks below possible: OpenTofu rejects sensitive import IDs ("The import id cannot be sensitive"), and the server's `cloudflare_account_id` variable is sensitive.
- **Import the existing objects, no downtime.** Recreating the tunnel would change its ID and token, and the DNS record can't be created next to the existing one. `iac/app` gets `import` blocks whose IDs are built from that data source and a per-workspace map of tunnel and DNS record IDs (not secret: the tunnel ID is public in the CNAME):

  | | tunnel | DNS record |
  |---|---|---|
  | dev | `8e6ad632-fbbd-470c-91c2-e9fc66534301` | `af5e6d0a3fb527271d0d3f2beb9c8af9` |
  | prod | `c612b46e-f87c-46ff-93cd-1b544c09cfd3` | `492171f03506aae7020d3ba240d4f2d7` |

  Each environment's deploy does its own import: dev on merge, prod with the next release. `iac/server` keeps managing the same objects with identical config until PR 2 forgets them with `removed` blocks.
- **The config has to match what Cloudflare returns.** That means `config_src = "cloudflare"` (the live value; `iac/server` leaves it at the default `local`, which the provider doesn't refresh) and no `tunnel_secret`. Cloudflare doesn't return the secret, so leaving it out gives no diff, and it's only needed for locally-managed tunnels. The `random_id.*_tunnel_secret`s therefore don't move.
- **Verified against the real dev objects.** I ran a read-only `tofu plan` (no apply) of the proposed config in a scratch module, with the import blocks and the zone data source, using the server's token. It gave `Plan: 3 to import, 0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy`, and the data source's tunnel token matched the one in the server state. The container's env doesn't change, so the import doesn't restart the tunnel. Without `config_src = "cloudflare"`, the tunnel planned an in-place update.

## Plan

### Prerequisite: let the server token create tokens

The server's account token gets `9109 Unauthorized` on `/accounts/<id>/tokens/permission_groups`. In the Cloudflare dashboard, add the account's API Tokens Write permission to it by hand. List that permission in README "Setup infrastructure".

### PR 1: manage the tunnel and DNS record in `iac/app`

- `iac/server/main.tf`:
  - `data "cloudflare_account_api_token_permission_groups_list"` for `Cloudflare Tunnel Write`, `DNS Write` and `Zone Read`. Confirm the names once the prerequisite is done.
  - `cloudflare_account_token.deploy` (`doedensonline-deploy`) with two policies: Tunnel Write on `com.cloudflare.api.account.<account_id>`, and DNS Write and Zone Read on `com.cloudflare.api.account.zone.<zone_id>`. `tofu validate` accepts this shape with provider 5.26.
  - `github_actions_secret` `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` from its `value`.
  - Apply by hand **before merging**: it adds the token and the secret, and changes nothing else.
- `iac/app/main.tf`:
  - Add `cloudflare = { source = "cloudflare/cloudflare", version = "~> 5.26" }` to `required_providers` and an empty `provider "cloudflare" {}`, and run `tofu init` to add it to `.terraform.lock.hcl`.
  - Add `hostname` to `local.environments` (`dev.doedensonline.nl`, `doedensonline.nl`).
  - Add `data "cloudflare_zone" "this"`, then `cloudflare_zero_trust_tunnel_cloudflared.this` (`name = local.name`, `config_src = "cloudflare"`), `cloudflare_zero_trust_tunnel_cloudflared_config.this` (ingress `local.env.hostname` → `http://localhost:${local.env.port}`, then `http_status:404`), `data "cloudflare_zero_trust_tunnel_cloudflared_token" "this"` and `cloudflare_dns_record.this` (proxied CNAME to `<tunnel id>.cfargotunnel.com`, `ttl = 1`). Copy the comments from `iac/server`.
  - Three `import` blocks with the IDs from the table above, in a local keyed by workspace.
  - `docker_container.cloudflared`: `TUNNEL_TOKEN` from the data source. Delete `variable "tunnel_token"` and its validation.
  - Update the header comment: the module now also manages the environment's tunnel and DNS record.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` deploy step: add `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}` and delete `TF_VAR_tunnel_token`.
- Docs:
  - README "Deploy manually": export `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (e.g. the server's token) and delete `-var tunnel_token=...`.
  - README "Setup infrastructure": a fresh environment gets its tunnel and DNS record with its first deploy.
  - CLAUDE.md: move "Cloudflare tunnels" from the `iac/server` bullet to the `iac/app` bullet.
- Testing: `tofu plan` from the PR branch in both workspaces, with the deployed image tag. Expect 3 imports and no changes to the tunnel, the config, the DNS record or the containers.
- Rollout: the merge imports dev, the next release imports prod. Check each deploy log for `3 imported` and no Cloudflare changes.

### PR 2: remove the tunnels from `iac/server` (after prod runs a release with PR 1)

- Commit 1:
  - `iac/server/main.tf`: replace the two tunnels, two tunnel configs, `cloudflare_dns_record.doedensonline`, `cloudflare_dns_record.doedensonline_dev` and the two `random_id.*_tunnel_secret`s with `removed` blocks (`lifecycle { destroy = false }`). Delete the token data sources and `DEV_TUNNEL_TOKEN` / `PROD_TUNNEL_TOKEN` from the secrets locals.
  - `iac/app/main.tf`: delete the `import` blocks and their ID map. They're no-ops for resources that are already in state; the deletion reaches prod with the next release.
  - Apply `iac/server` by hand: the plan forgets the 8 resources and destroys the 2 `github_actions_secret`s, nothing else.
- Commit 2: delete the `removed` blocks. This changes no state, so it needs no apply.

## Side effects

- **CI gets Cloudflare access.** A leaked `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` could change any record in the zone (including the SES DKIM and verification records) and create or delete any tunnel in the account. CI already has root SSH to the host and ECR push, so the new exposure is mostly DNS.
- **Rolling back across PR 1** by re-running an old deploy job would plan to destroy the tunnel, its config and the DNS record, since the old config doesn't have them. It should fail before that, because the old job has no Cloudflare token, but don't rely on that. Roll back across PR 1 by deploying the old image tag with the current `iac/app` (README "Deploy manually") instead.
- **Fresh tunnels are created without a `tunnel_secret`,** so Cloudflare generates one. That's fine for remotely-managed tunnels but isn't tested here, because the imports never create a tunnel.
- **Out of scope:** with the ingress next to the containers, `cloudflared` could reach the app over a per-environment Docker network (`http://doedensonline-<env>:8080`), dropping `network_mode = "host"` and the published host port. Expiry or rotation of the deploy token is also out of scope.

items.title: Generate secret_key_base in iac/app
items.body:
Each environment's `secret_key_base` is generated in `iac/server` (`random_id.dev_secret_key_base` / `random_id.prod_secret_key_base`), published as the `DEV_SECRET_KEY_BASE` / `PROD_SECRET_KEY_BASE` GitHub Actions secrets, passed to `iac/app` as `TF_VAR_secret_key_base`, and only used there as the containers' `SECRET_KEY_BASE`. Generating it in `iac/app` removes the variable, two secrets and their CI plumbing, and lets each environment own its key. Unlike moving the tunnels (see the side effects in #269), it needs no new credentials in CI: the `random` provider has none.

## Design

- **One `random_id` per workspace.** `iac/app` gets `random_id.secret_key_base` with `byte_length = 64` and passes `.hex` to the containers, the same as `iac/server` does now. The dev and prod workspaces each hold their own key in their state.
- **Import the existing keys, don't rotate them.** The app uses the cookie session store, so a new key would log everyone out. Importing keeps the value, so the containers' env doesn't change and the first deploy doesn't replace them because of it. Verified locally with OpenTofu 1.13 and random 3.9.1: importing a `random_id`'s `b64_url` into a `random_id` with `byte_length = 64` gives the same `hex` and a plan with no changes.
- **`tofu import` by hand, not an `import` block.** The import ID is the key itself (its `b64_url`), so an `import` block would put it in the repo. The ID is read from the server state into a shell variable, so it doesn't end up in the shell history either.
- **Two PRs, like #269.** `iac/server` keeps the secrets until prod runs a release with PR 1, since prod deploys from release tags and keeps reading `PROD_SECRET_KEY_BASE` until then.
- **`removed` with `destroy = false` in `iac/server`.** Destroying a `random_id` only touches state anyway, but a plan that says "forget" instead of "destroy" for the live keys is easier to check.

## Plan

### PR 1: generate the key in `iac/app`

- `iac/app/main.tf`:
  - Add `random = { source = "hashicorp/random", version = "~> 3.6" }` to `required_providers`, the same constraint as `iac/server`.
  - Add `resource "random_id" "secret_key_base" { byte_length = 64 }`, with a comment that 64 bytes give 128 hex characters, the same length as `bin/rails secret`.
  - `local.container_env`: `SECRET_KEY_BASE=${random_id.secret_key_base.hex}`.
  - Delete `variable "secret_key_base"`.
- `iac/app/.terraform.lock.hcl`: run `tofu init` to add `hashicorp/random`.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: delete `TF_VAR_secret_key_base` from the deploy step.
- README "Deploy manually": delete `-var secret_key_base=...`.
- Rollout, **right before merging**, from the PR branch, for `dev` and then `prod`:

  ```
  cd iac/app
  tofu workspace select dev
  id=$(tofu -chdir=../server show -json | jq -r '.values.root_module.resources[] | select(.address == "random_id.dev_secret_key_base") | .values.b64_url')
  tofu import -var image_tag=... -var ssh_host=... -var smtp_host=... -var smtp_username=... -var smtp_password=... -var tunnel_token=... random_id.secret_key_base "$id"
  tofu plan -var image_tag=... ...
  ```

  Use the image tag that's deployed now (`tofu state show docker_image.app`), so the plan shouldn't touch the app container. If it replaces the app container because of `env`, the key differs: don't merge.
- Until the merge, master's `iac/app` doesn't have the resource yet. A dev deploy from another merge in between drops it from the dev state (the running key is unaffected, since it still comes from the secret), so redo the dev import if one ran. Don't publish a release between the prod import and the merge.
- After the merge, the dev deploy log shouldn't show `random_id.secret_key_base` being created; the same goes for prod with the next release.

### PR 2: remove the keys from `iac/server` (after prod runs a release with PR 1)

- Commit 1: replace `random_id.dev_secret_key_base` and `random_id.prod_secret_key_base` with `removed` blocks (`lifecycle { destroy = false }`), and delete `DEV_SECRET_KEY_BASE` / `PROD_SECRET_KEY_BASE` from `github_actions_{dev,prod}_secrets` along with the outdated "Rails 4.0 secret_key_base" comment. Apply by hand: the plan forgets the two `random_id`s and destroys the two `github_actions_secret`s, nothing else.
- Commit 2: delete the `removed` blocks. This changes no state, so it needs no apply.

## Side effects

- Each key lives only in its `iac/app` workspace state, which already holds the SMTP password and tunnel token. Losing or recreating a workspace's state generates a new key, which logs everyone out of that environment.
- Rotating a key becomes a per-environment `tofu apply -replace=random_id.secret_key_base` in `iac/app` and doesn't touch `iac/server`.
- Rolling back across PR 1 (re-running a deploy job from before it) runs the old `iac/app`, which drops `random_id.secret_key_base` from the workspace state, so the next deploy generates a new key unless it's imported again. After PR 2, the old deploy job also gets an empty `TF_VAR_secret_key_base`, because the secret is gone.

items.title: Set up Cloudflare IaC
items.body:
## User value

As the homelab operator, I want the remaining existing Cloudflare DNS configuration managed declaratively so that the zone is reproducible and drift is visible without changing working ingress or email delivery.

## Verified repository context

Cloudflare IaC already exists:

- `terraform/domains.tf` manages the swarmpit, portainer, and jenkins CNAMEs.
- `terraform/tunnels.tf` manages the VPS shield tunnel, ingress rules, and test CNAME.
- The provider constraint is `~> 4.0`; the lockfile resolves Cloudflare 4.52.9.
- `docs/iac_audit_and_roadmap.md` identifies remaining manually managed DNS records for Pages, home tunnels, SendGrid, and ImprovMX.

The roadmap inventory is historical. Re-read the live zone rather than treating its record count as current.

## Scope and constraints

Complete the existing DNS adoption as one concern by importing remaining in-scope records into the existing Terraform configuration. Inventory the live zone first and record explicitly excluded records. Preserve all already-managed DNS and VPS tunnel resources.

Use the locked Cloudflare 4.52.9 schema and import contract. Exact-version registry documentation, the installed binary's matching source revision, and a live CNAME import have now been checked. DNS import IDs use `<zone_id>/<record_id>`. Use `content` for new declarations; `value` is deprecated. Confirm the attributes and behavior of every actual in-scope record type before extending the CNAME findings.

Do not combine DNS adoption with a provider major upgrade, tunnel redesign, Pages application deployment, broad account/WAF/Access management, remote-state migration, or enabling automatic applies. Those are separate changes if required. Use least-privilege API credentials and keep secrets/state outside Git.

## Verified import behavior and candidate workaround

Checked on 2026-10-11 using the live Portainer CNAME and isolated temporary local state:

- A currently configured API token successfully read both the zone and DNS record. The earlier Wrangler OAuth credential could read the zone but lacked DNS-record access. Credential availability is no longer the current blocker; verify least-privilege Zone Read and DNS Read permissions for adoption.
- Provider 4.52.9 successfully imported the existing record and preserved its identity. `task tf:validate` also passed for the existing repository configuration, with existing tunnel deprecation warnings.
- The imported `value`, `content`, and `allow_overwrite` attributes were null. Both `value` and `content` declarations matching the live record produced an in-place update in a normal plan (exit code 2), without any replacement or deletion.
- A refresh-only reconciliation did not populate these fields: the subsequent normal plan still proposed the update. Declarative import blocks also retained the proposed update. An empty refresh-only plan does not satisfy the adoption acceptance criterion.
- In temporary state, setting missing `content` from a fresh Cloudflare API response and setting `allow_overwrite` to the configured default of false produced an empty normal plan (exit code 0).
- A later intentional configuration change to `content` still produced an update, proving this workaround preserved change detection for the tested CNAME.
- The live record's API representation remained unchanged throughout the tests. All test state was removed; no production state was repaired and no normal apply was executed.

The candidate procedure for preserving the original no-change-plan requirement is a narrowly reviewed repair of missing imported attributes. Back up state, verify the exact zone/record identity and current API values, preserve unrelated state, keep state locking and lineage/serial safeguards enabled, and require a normal plan with zero changes afterward. Do not use forced state pushes or `ignore_changes` to conceal DNS differences. Manual state updates are exceptional operations; design and review the production procedure before executing it.

This workaround is proven only for one CNAME. Verify the inventory's other record types, including email records and their type-specific attributes, before generalizing it. A normal apply that rewrites matching DNS content is an alternative with a Cloudflare write; that path has not been tested or approved by this investigation.

## Acceptance criteria

- Given the live zone and Terraform state, when the inventory is reconciled, then every DNS record is classified already managed, to import, or intentionally excluded with a reason.
- Given existing records, when in-scope resources are declared and imported, then a normal plan reports no changes, replacements, or deletions and `plan -detailed-exitcode` returns 0; an empty refresh-only plan is insufficient.
- Given imported attributes require reconciliation, when the reviewed procedure runs, then record identities and unrelated state remain intact, backups and locking are preserved, and a later intentional configuration change is still detected without `ignore_changes`.
- Given existing DNS and tunnel behavior, when adoption is verified, then names, types, values, TTLs, proxy flags, MX priorities, and tunnel ingress remain unchanged.
- Given Pages, home tunnel, and email DNS entries in scope, when post-import checks run, then DNS answers match the captured baseline and current application routes continue working.
- Given the adopted configuration, when `task tf:fmt`, `task tf:validate`, and `task tf:plan` run, then checks succeed and state/credentials remain untracked.

## Tasks

- [ ] Inventory the live zone read-only and compare against declarations/state.
- [x] Verify exact-version schema/import contract and live CNAME import behavior against locked provider 4.52.9.
- [x] Test refresh-only, declarative import, and the candidate state repair in isolated CNAME state; verify a no-change normal plan and detection of a later content change.
- [ ] Verify import and reconciliation behavior for every actual in-scope record type; do not infer complete coverage from the CNAME test.
- [ ] Add only missing in-scope DNS declarations, preserving complete live record attributes.
- [ ] Prepare and review the bounded adoption/state-reconciliation procedure with backups, identity checks, locking, rollback, and preserved lineage/serial safeguards.
- [ ] Import in-scope resources, reconcile only reviewed missing state fields where required, and verify a no-change normal plan before any live DNS apply.
- [ ] Check DNS/routing baseline parity and preserve existing tunnel identifiers and credentials.
- [ ] Update the IaC inventory and document import, validation, diagnostics, and rollback under docs/ and README.
- [ ] Deliver one single-concern draft PR; do not close until every in-scope record is adopted and verified.

## References

[Existing VPS tunnel resources](https://github.com/gordonpn/server-services-configs/blob/master/terraform/tunnels.tf)

items.title: [2026.11 14/18] Agent skill and Claude Code plugin
items.body:
> Part of #81 (azctx 2026.11 release). Stack layer **14 of 18**.
> Branch `2026.11/14-ai-agents`, stacked on `2026.11/13-env-guard` (#94). Next layer: #96.

## Context

AI agents increasingly run Azure commands for developers. They tend to call `az account set`, which changes the subscription for every terminal of the user, because the Azure CLI has no per-process override. Agent Skills are an open format supported by Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, Cursor and others. Claude Code plugins can bundle a skill with a `PreToolUse` hook that blocks a Bash command, and a GitHub repository can serve as a plugin marketplace.

## Scope

- [ ] `skills/azctx/SKILL.md` in the Agent Skills format, short, versioned with the CLI. It tells an agent to:
  - read the context with `azctx -c -o json` and `azctx list -o json` before any Azure action
  - never switch the global default on its own. Pass `--subscription <id>` to `az` commands and use `azctx exec` for Terraform, azd and SDK based tools
  - run `azctx guard` before changes and stop on exit code 4
  - leave `azctx login`, `azctx auth broker` and `--yes` for protected subscriptions to the user
  - read exit codes and JSON errors (layer 07)
- [ ] Claude Code plugin in the repository: `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` plus a plugin directory with the skill and an optional `PreToolUse` hook (`hooks/hooks.json`, matcher `Bash`). The hook runs `azctx guard` before commands starting with `az`, `azd`, `terraform` or `bicep` and blocks with exit code 2 and a reason when the guard fails. Without `azctx` on the `PATH` or without `.azctx.yaml`, it lets the command through with a one-line notice.
- [ ] Test that every `azctx` command in `SKILL.md`, `AGENTS.md` and the docs exists and parses, and that the plugin and marketplace manifests are valid JSON with the required fields. Part of `make check`.
- [ ] `docs/ai-agents.md` (draft): installing the skill in Claude Code (`/plugin marketplace add whiteducksoftware/azctx`), GitHub Copilot, Codex and Cursor, the hook, `.azctx.yaml`, and the limits. Layer 18 finalizes it.
- [ ] The docs state that guard, skill and protected subscriptions reduce mistakes but are no security boundary. Access control stays with Azure RBAC, PIM and Conditional Access.

## Out of scope

An MCP server. Agents call the CLI directly, the Azure MCP Server covers resource operations.

## Ground rules

- azctx never reads or writes credentials or the MSAL token cache.
- `make check` passes before the PR leaves draft.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `claude plugin validate .` passes (run manually, noted in the PR).
- [ ] Hook script tests for allow, block and missing azctx.
- [ ] The agent files test runs in CI.

## Sources

- [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification)
- [Claude Code hooks: `PreToolUse`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks)
- [Claude Code plugin marketplaces](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces)
- [GitHub Copilot agent skills](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/about-agent-skills)
- [Azure MCP Server](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/developer/azure-mcp-server/overview)

## Go-live related

AI agents work in the right Azure context without changing the user's global default or deploying to the wrong subscription.

items.title: azctx 2026.11 release: current Azure CLI, CI/CD and AI agent support

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
## Summary

This feature delivers the azctx 2026.11 release. It brings azctx up to date with the current Azure CLI (2.61 and later), with broker based sign-in on Windows and macOS and with mandatory MFA across many tenants. It also adds features that go beyond the Azure CLI, including support for CI/CD pipelines and AI agents, and moves the toolchain, dependencies, CI and release pipeline to a maintained state.

The release removes everything that is no longer needed without a deprecation period. Version: `2026.11.0`, release candidates `2026.11.0-rc.N`.

Code owners: @nmeisenzahl, @hutstep, @swolg.

## Why

| Area | Today (2024.12.5, last commit March 2025) |
| --- | --- |
| Toolchain | Go 1.23.6 is out of support. Supported releases are Go 1.27 and 1.26 |
| Security | govulncheck reports 35 reachable vulnerabilities (Go standard library, `golang.org/x/text` v0.21.0) |
| Tests | None |
| Azure CLI | Built before the 2.61 login experience. Keeps its own tenant cache although `azureProfile.json` now carries tenant names |
| Auth | Assumes a browser login. Device code output is swallowed. MFA detection is a substring search for "mfa" |
| Bugs | Tenant cache corruption, duplicate subscription names collapse, `azctx -` not implemented, offline runs fail after a successful switch, device code invisible, noisy output |
| Maintenance | 10 Dependabot PRs open, golangci-lint config incompatible with the version CI uses |

## Value on top of the Azure CLI

Since 2.61 the Azure CLI shows a subscription picker during `az login`. azctx stays useful because of:

| Task | Azure CLI | azctx after this release |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Switch later in the day | `az account set --subscription <id or exact name>` | Fuzzy picker at any time, `azctx prod`, `azctx contoso/prod`, IDs |
| Same name in several tenants | Fails with "has more than one match" | Candidates shown with tenant names |
| Previous subscription | Not available | `azctx -` |
| Short names | Not available | Aliases, pinned and recently used subscriptions |
| Many tenants with MFA | Warning per failed tenant, manual `az login --tenant <id>` each | `azctx login` retries only the failed tenants after one confirmation |
| Broker sign-in | Three manual steps | `azctx auth broker enable` |
| Diagnostics | Several commands and files | `azctx doctor` |
| Terraform, azd, pipelines | Export variables by hand | `azctx env`, `azctx exec`, GitHub Actions and Azure DevOps formats |
| Wrong subscription | Not prevented | `azctx guard`, `.azctx.yaml`, protected subscriptions |
| AI agents | Agents run `az account set` and change the default for every terminal | Agent skill, JSON errors, `--no-input`, guard hook for Claude Code, `azctx history` |

azctx never signs in itself and never handles tokens. Authentication stays in the Azure CLI.

## Guiding principles

- azctx never reads or writes credentials or the MSAL token cache, and never writes `azureProfile.json` or anything else in `AZURE_CONFIG_DIR`.
- Follow the Azure CLI, do not shadow it.
- A side task such as the update check never fails a successful switch.
- Every interactive flow has a non-interactive form with stable output.
- Clean break: legacy flags, files and fallbacks are removed, not deprecated.
- The CLI contract (commands, flags, output formats, exit codes, config schema) ships complete with this release.

## Delivery: one stack of pull requests

Every implementation task below is one pull request. The pull requests form a single [GitHub stack](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/reference/stacked-pull-requests) on top of `main`, in the order of the table. No release is published while the stack is open. The release task runs after the stack is merged.

| Layer | Sub-issue | Branch | Stacked on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 01 | #82 | `2026.11/01-toolchain` | `main` |
| 02 | #83 | `2026.11/02-ci` | layer 01 |
| 03 | #84 | `2026.11/03-structure` | layer 02 |
| 04 | #85 | `2026.11/04-contributing` | layer 03 |
| 05 | #86 | `2026.11/05-dependencies` | layer 04 |
| 06 | #87 | `2026.11/06-bugfixes` | layer 05 |
| 07 | #88 | `2026.11/07-cli-contract` | layer 06 |
| 08 | #89 | `2026.11/08-azure-cli` | layer 07 |
| 09 | #90 | `2026.11/09-auth` | layer 08 |
| 10 | #91 | `2026.11/10-mfa-login` | layer 09 |
| 11 | #92 | `2026.11/11-config-selection` | layer 10 |
| 12 | #93 | `2026.11/12-tenants-history` | layer 11 |
| 13 | #94 | `2026.11/13-env-guard` | layer 12 |
| 14 | #95 | `2026.11/14-ai-agents` | layer 13 |
| 15 | #96 | `2026.11/15-hardening` | layer 14 |
| 16 | #97 | `2026.11/16-integration-tests` | layer 15 |
| 17 | #98 | `2026.11/17-release-pipeline` | layer 16 |
| 18 | #99 | `2026.11/18-docs` | layer 17 |
| Release | #100 | none, tag on `main` | stack merged |

### Working with the stack

```sh
gh extension install github/gh-stack
gh stack init                       # name the first branch 2026.11/01-toolchain
gh stack add 2026.11/02-ci          # one branch per layer, in table order
gh stack push
gh stack submit                     # opens or updates the pull requests as a linked stack
gh stack rebase && gh stack push    # after a lower layer changes
```

Rules:

- Each pull request references its sub-issue with `Closes #<sub-issue>` and this feature issue with `Part of #81`.
- Reviews, required checks and CODEOWNERS are evaluated against `main` for every layer. Each layer needs one code owner approval.
- Squash merge. Lower layers can merge as soon as they are approved, GitHub rebases and retargets the rest. Merging the top layer merges every layer below it in one step.
- A stack needs linear history between its branches. Use `gh stack rebase` or **Rebase stack** in the merge box.
- Stacked PRs are in preview. If the feature is not available for the repository, request access at gh.io/stacksbeta or fall back to classic stacked pull requests (each pull request targets the branch of the layer below).
- Every user-visible change adds a row to `docs/upgrade.md` in the same pull request.
- A hotfix for 2024.12.5 users goes to a `release/2024.12` branch created from the `2024.12.5` tag, never to the stack.

## Breaking changes (summary)

The full list lives in `docs/upgrade.md` and becomes the top of the release notes.

- Homebrew formula replaced by a cask, Homebrew on Linux no longer published, macOS binaries unsigned.
- 32 bit `windows/arm` dropped, because Go removed the port. Windows on ARM64 stays supported. macOS 13 and Windows 10 or later required.
- Azure CLI 2.61.0 or later required.
- Removed: `--short`, `--filter-tenant-level`, `login --force-mfa`, `azctxTenants.json`, log style output, `version -o yaml|pretty|short`.
- Disabled subscriptions, tenant level accounts and other clouds hidden by default.
- Fixed exit codes, non-interactive runs fail instead of waiting for input.

## Decisions

| Topic | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Version | `2026.11.0`, no deprecation period for removed behavior |
| Picker | bubbletea with bubbles and lipgloss |
| Switching | Always through `az account set` |
| Distribution | GitHub Releases, Homebrew cask (macOS), Chocolatey, winget. Linux: release binaries only |
| macOS signing | Unsigned binaries, quarantine removal through a declared cask step |
| Code owners | @nmeisenzahl, @hutstep, @swolg, also the required reviewers of the `release` environment |
| Workload identities | No own managed identity or federated credential flows. Pass through to `az login` |
| winget | PR to `microsoft/winget-pkgs` opened manually from the fork branch |
| Chocolatey key | `CHOCO_API_KEY` from the `hutstep` Chocolatey account, rotated into the `release` environment |
| Update notice | 2024.12.5 needs no change. The release is published without the latest flag and marked as latest once Chocolatey and winget are live |
| Contributor instructions | One lean `AGENTS.md`, no tool specific instruction files |
| AI agents | Agent skill plus Claude Code plugin with a guard hook. No MCP server |
| Delivery | All implementation in this repository first, publishing as the last step |

## Prerequisites

- [ ] **Test tenants** for layer 10 and layer 16: at least three tenants, two enforcing MFA, plus one federated service principal.

## Out of scope

PIM activation, AKS integration, an MCP server, a dedicated GitHub Action, a container image, self-update.

## Sources

- [Sign in interactively with the Azure CLI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/authenticate-azure-cli-web-account-manager)
- [Impact of MFA on the Azure CLI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/authenticate-azure-cli-mfa)
- [Plan for mandatory Microsoft Entra MFA](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-mandatory-multifactor-authentication)
- [Azure CLI core HISTORY.rst](https://github.com/Azure/azure-cli/blob/dev/src/azure-cli-core/HISTORY.rst)
- [Go release history](https://go.dev/doc/devel/release)
- [GitHub stacked pull requests](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/reference/stacked-pull-requests) and [gh-stack](https://github.github.com/gh-stack/introduction/overview/)
- [Homebrew 7.0.0](https://brew.sh/2026/09/13/homebrew-7.0.0/)

## Go-live related

Keeps azctx usable with current Azure CLI sign-in and MFA requirements and removes known vulnerabilities from shipped binaries.

items.title: Coordinate shared VM ingress, Notoli migration, and MacroMapper launch

labels.name: docker
labels.description: Pull requests that update docker code

labels.name: nginx
labels.description: Shared ingress proxy and Nginx configuration

items.body:
## Deployment reconciliation — 2026-10-11

**Production deployment complete; coordination issue remains open for outstanding acceptance.** On 2026-10-11 Agent03 accepted Infrastructure source `6819c1c47b14e00a023d8a86aa30cb00bfa9b5a7` (production deployment record `7002270103`), Notoli source `05835a38b3ff0aafd6d89c060055a1ffa7d251d5`, and MacroMapper source `9345c365a0e9e1f1a8e949d4108185e22ddffe73`. PRs Infra #11/#12/#13/#15, Notoli #906/#908/#907, and MacroMapper #242/#244/#243 were merged. Both apps passed initial and independent repeat GitHub Actions deployments, origin/public/API/MCP probes, database snapshot and isolated-restore checks, recovery retention, and deployment isolation. Cloudflare remained unchanged. Agent03 completed targeted cleanup (203.68 MiB reclaimed) without global prune. #15's source reconciliation did not reload/recreate ingress because gateway config was byte-identical. [Original rollout report](https://github.com/VanillaIceCube/JudeAndrewAlabaInfrastructure/issues/4#issuecomment-6113551888) · [final activation](https://github.com/VanillaIceCube/JudeAndrewAlabaInfrastructure/issues/4#issuecomment-6114144231).

**Still open / not validated:** fresh registration/login and OAuth consent; MacroMapper end-to-end meal CRUD, per-user isolation, password-reset email and AI estimation; host reboot and live rollback; recurring off-host backups/ongoing monitoring; Notoli port 3000 disposition; Infrastructure advanced CI/security/review bots (#5–#9), project schema (#3), and gateway Actions automation (#14). Existing authenticated Notoli MCP connectivity was checked read-only only.

---

## ⛔ MASTER COORDINATION — Shared VM infrastructure and four-agent delivery

**Owner decision (2026-10-11): This is the canonical, central coordination issue for the entire multi-application deployment effort.** All four agents must use **this issue's comment thread** for cross-repository architecture, VM observations, blockers, decisions, and rollout handoffs. This **supersedes all earlier instructions in the Notoli and MacroMapper issue descriptions/comments** saying that Notoli #904 is the main coordination thread. Their scopes remain active, but the discussion hub moves here.

**Absolute rule: NO MERGES WITHOUT EXPLICIT OWNER APPROVAL, including Dependabot; NO production changes without separate, explicit owner approval.** A ticket assignment, bot approval, passing CI, agent agreement, a comment, or the previous unauthorized merge of MacroMapper PR #239 is never approval. No auto-merge, bypass, direct release-branch pushes, CI-triggered deployments, or hidden VM mutation. Work in feature branches and stop at a reviewable PR. The owner must authorize each PR merge individually, and authorize production rollout separately.

### Goals and boundaries
- Deploy MacroMapper as its existing application on the same DigitalOcean VM as **currently working Notoli**, without expanding product functionality or breaking Notoli.
- Establish a **host-owned, version-controlled Nginx ingress** and shared network conventions, independent of app release cycles. Cloudflare continues to provide external DNS/proxy/TLS behavior.
- Keep Notoli, MacroMapper, and later apps independently deployable, with private backends, dedicated networks/storage/secrets, reproducible app CI/CD, safe backups and rollback.
- **This repository owns shared infrastructure source code.** `JudeAndrewAlabaWebsite` remains its own website application; neither app repository owns the gateway long-term. Avoid unnecessary Kubernetes/Terraform/Traefik frameworks for a single VM.
- The infrastructure repo inherits the **same full bot/security engineering standard** as Notoli, MacroMapper and FullStackTemplate, adapted to the actual infrastructure language/configuration. Do not weaken reviews or security to save setup time.

### Linked implementation tickets (each retains its own scope)
| Workstream | Ticket | Owner / deliverable |
|---|---|---|
| Shared ingress implementation | [Infrastructure #1](https://github.com/VanillaIceCube/JudeAndrewAlabaInfrastructure/issues/1) | Agent 4; Nginx/Compose/network/config/rollback PR |
| Infrastructure repo automation | [Infrastructure #2](https://github.com/VanillaIceCube/JudeAndrewAlabaInfrastructure/issues/2) | Full CI/CodeQL/Dependabot/security/review-bot parity; **no auto-merge** |
| GitHub Project setup | [Infrastructure #3](https://github.com/VanillaIceCube/JudeAndrewAlabaInfrastructure/issues/3) | Board fields/views/automation/labels/rulesets/app access |
| Notoli app migration | [Notoli #904](https://github.com/VanillaIceCube/Notoli/issues/904) | Agent 1; preserve working Notoli, trusted proxy, release isolation |
| MacroMapper app integration | [MacroMapper #240](https://github.com/VanillaIceCube/MacroMapper/issues/240) | Agent 2; audit PR #239, simplify deployment, verify launch |
| Earlier launch scope | [MacroMapper #236](https://github.com/VanillaIceCube/MacroMapper/issues/236), [#238](https://github.com/VanillaIceCube/MacroMapper/issues/238) | Existing application acceptance requirements |

### Four distinct agent roles
1. **Agent 1 — Notoli repository agent:** own Notoli-only repository changes, diagnose deployment/proxy trust and MCP/OAuth requirements, review infrastructure contract, plan nondisruptive migration. No shared gateway code in Notoli.
2. **Agent 2 — MacroMapper repository agent:** audit merged-but-unauthorized [PR #239](https://github.com/VanillaIceCube/MacroMapper/pull/239); recommend keep/simplify/replace/revert for each relevant component; own MacroMapper-only changes and review shared interface. No control of Notoli's gateway.
3. **Agent 3 — VM resident agent:** read-only live environment authority until explicitly authorized otherwise. Inspect containers, Compose labels, ports, Docker networks, gateway/TLS metadata, storage, RAM/disk/swap, deployment drift, backups/rollback readiness; redact sensitive values. Once separately approved, **sole production operator**, sequentially, with an approved runbook. No ad hoc Docker or Nginx changes while auditing.
4. **Agent 4 — Infrastructure repository agent:** own gateway Nginx config, ingress Compose/network definitions, validation checks and operational runbooks in THIS repo, and infrastructure code PRs. Incorporate the other three agents' evidence; do not merge or operate the VM. Full repository bot/security standard is a separate prerequisite tracked in #2. If Agent 4 has not yet been provisioned, work remains blocked at that handoff; do not pretend the agent exists.

**GitHub issue comments are asynchronous—not live messaging.** Reading or posting a comment does not automatically wake another agent. Every agent must re-read this issue's latest comments at decision/implementation checkpoints; if a tool cannot post, give the owner a sanitized Markdown comment to relay.

### Message protocol — post cross-cutting messages ONLY HERE
- `[VM AUDIT]` — Agent 3's inspected live state, observation time, evidence, unknowns, sanitized paths (never env contents/private keys).
- `[VM RECONCILIATION]` — Agent 1 maps live Notoli behavior and its network/proxy trust expectations to the proposed design.
- `[ARCH QUESTION]` — any agent identifies a shared dependency/blocker; include context, options, recommended resolution and specific responding agent.
- `[ARCH RESPONSE]` — response in this issue with evidence or alternative and affected workstreams.
- `[ARCH CONTRACT — PROPOSED]` — Agent 4 consolidates the **versioned** contract (Agent 1 coordinates Notoli compatibility). Not approved until owner explicitly says so here.
- `[CONTRACT REVIEW]` — Agents 1 and 2 independently validate app compatibility and list objections/acceptance evidence.
- `[VM FEASIBILITY REVIEW]` — Agent 3 validates the contract against observed VM state, capacity, permissions, migration safety and rollback.
- `[BLOCKED — OWNER DECISION]` — explicit outstanding decision; no implicit default.
- `[IMPLEMENTATION HANDOFF]` — each repository agent posts PR links, change summary, validation logs, exact contract version, risks and dependencies. Also cross-reference from its own implementation issue.
- `[AWAITING OWNER MERGE APPROVAL]` — stop point for each PR.
- `[DEPLOYMENT PLAN — OWNER APPROVAL REQUIRED]` — Agent 3 posts an exact operational plan, proposed effects, backups, acceptance and rollback commands; wait for explicit deployment permission.
- `[DEPLOYMENT RESULT]` and `[PRODUCTION HANDOFF]` — Agent 3 documents verification, image SHAs, restoration readiness and remaining risks.

Keep application-specific implementation conversations in #904/#240 and infrastructure-specific code discussions in #1/#2/#3, but **link decisions and post summaries here**; don't create parallel, conflicting architecture discussions.

### Explicit migration from old discussion hub
- Previous central discussion lived on [Notoli #904](https://github.com/VanillaIceCube/Notoli/issues/904). **Treat it as historical context only, not the active architecture thread.** Agents should read its body and prior comments for context and bring all *still unresolved* questions and latest evidence to this issue.
- Do not silently ignore any previous VM audits or contracts already posted on Notoli #904; summarize and link them here, label their owner-approval status, and seek reconfirmation where required.
- A comment stating that the coordination hub moved is to be posted on **Notoli #904** and **MacroMapper #240**. Those original issue descriptions must not be edited.

### Critical design checks before contract approval
- Current public :80/:443 ownership, actual Nginx container/Compose config and vhost routes; Cloudflare origin certificates; independent service names and networks.
- Notoli's exact trusted-proxy model (historically proxy `172.30.88.2`, backend `172.30.88.3`) and MCP/OAuth forwarding/headers must survive cutover. Avoid silently relaxing trust or replacing running containers.
- Review and decouple host-global `docker system prune -af`, shared proxy recreation, cross-app Compose overrides, `env-prod` release side effects and other shared-host hazards.
- Check available VM memory/disk and backups before adding load; historical ~2 GiB figure **requires live confirmation**.
- MacroMapper PR #239 exists on `main` because Codex reportedly merged it without authorization. Treat it as **unreviewed candidate**, not accepted architecture or proof of deployment.
- Do not expose app backends, databases, keys or cert private keys in the repository, CI logs or issue comments.

### Review/deployment sequence
- [x] VM agent submits sanitized live audit **here**.
- [x] Notoli and MacroMapper agents perform read-only app audits and review VM observations.
- [x] Infrastructure Agent 4 proposes shared contract; Agent 1/2 review, VM agent feasibility-checks, all outstanding disputes recorded here.
- [x] Owner explicitly approves the final contract.
- [x] Each agent prepares focused feature-branch PR(s); standard CI/bots/security checks run; **owner explicitly authorizes each merge**.
- [x] VM agent writes cutover/rollback plan; owner separately authorizes live actions.
- [x] Execute shared gateway + Notoli transition; verify current Notoli workflows (especially MCP/OAuth) and rollback capability before proceeding.
- [ ] Deploy MacroMapper; verify app functionality, both sites, independent redeploy capability, persistence, backups, and monitoring.
- [x] Record complete production handoff; close tickets only on observed acceptance, not merely green CI.

**No automatic merges or production actions are authorized by creating this coordination issue.**

items.title: 🤖 Set up Dependabot for automated dependency updates
items.body:
## 🤖 Hey team! Let's set up Dependabot 👋

Hi there! 👋

I'm here from the **Advisense Platform Team** with a small but mighty improvement for this repo. We're rolling out **automated dependency updates** across the organization — because life's too short to manually chase CVEs on a Friday afternoon. ☕

### What's happening?

We'd like to add (or update) a `.github/dependabot.yml` configuration so that:

- 📦 Dependencies stay fresh with **weekly** pull requests (every Monday — start the week with clean deps!)
- 🧹 Updates are **grouped** so you don't get buried in 47 individual PRs for a single framework bump
- 🐳 Docker base images stay up to date (if you're using Docker)
- ⚙️ GitHub Actions workflows use the latest versions of their actions
- 🔒 Security patches land automatically instead of gathering dust

### What we need you to do

**Nothing!** 🎉 Copilot will analyze this repo and create a PR with the right configuration. All you need to do is **review and merge** when it shows up.

If you already have a `dependabot.yml` — no worries! Copilot will check what's there and only add what's missing. Your existing setup won't be touched unnecessarily.

If this repo turns out to have **no dependencies at all** (no package managers, no Docker, no GitHub Actions) — Copilot will simply close this issue and let you know. No action needed, nothing to worry about. Not every repo needs this, and that's perfectly fine! 🙂

---

### 🔧 Instructions for Copilot

Please analyze this repository and create or update `.github/dependabot.yml`:

1. **Detect all ecosystems** by examining the repository structure:

   **Python** — pick the correct ecosystem based on what the project actually uses:
   - `uv` → if you find `uv.lock` or `[tool.uv]` in `pyproject.toml`
   - `pip` → if you find `requirements.txt`, `setup.py`, `setup.cfg`, or a `pyproject.toml` without `[tool.uv]` and without `[tool.poetry]`
   - ⚠️ Do NOT default to `pip` if the project uses `uv`. Use `"uv"` as the `package-ecosystem` value — Dependabot supports it natively.

   **JavaScript/TypeScript** — always use `npm` (Dependabot handles npm, yarn, and pnpm lock files under the `npm` ecosystem).

   **Other ecosystems** — detect by marker files:
   - `*.csproj` / `*.fsproj` / `*.sln` / `packages.config` → `nuget`
   - `pom.xml` → `maven`
   - `build.gradle` / `build.gradle.kts` → `gradle`
   - `go.mod` → `gomod`
   - `Cargo.toml` → `cargo`
   - `composer.json` → `composer`
   - `Gemfile` → `bundler`
   - `*.tf` files with provider blocks → `terraform`
   - `pubspec.yaml` → `pub`
   - `Package.swift` → `swift`
   - `mix.exs` → `mix`

   **Docker** — look for:
   - `Dockerfile`, `*.Dockerfile`
   - `docker-compose.yml`, `docker-compose.yaml`, `compose.yml`, `compose.yaml`

   **GitHub Actions** — look for any `.yml` / `.yaml` files in `.github/workflows/`.

2. **Handle monorepos correctly**: if package manager files exist in subdirectories (e.g., `frontend/package.json`, `backend/pyproject.toml`, `services/api/Dockerfile`), create separate entries with the correct `directory` path for each location. Do NOT just use `"/"` if the files are in subdirectories.

3. **Configure each ecosystem entry** with:
   - `schedule: interval: "weekly"` and `day: "monday"`
   - `open-pull-requests-limit: 10`
   - Grouped updates using the `groups` key:
     - For ecosystems that distinguish production/development dependencies (npm, pip, uv, bundler, composer): create two groups — `production-dependencies` with `dependency-type: "production"` and `development-dependencies` with `dependency-type: "development"`
     - For all other ecosystems (docker, github-actions, terraform, gomod, cargo, maven, gradle, nuget, pub, swift, mix): create one group with `patterns: ["*"]`

4. **Always include** a `github-actions` entry if `.github/workflows/` contains any workflow files.

5. **If `.github/dependabot.yml` already exists**: read it carefully, preserve all existing configuration, and only add entries for ecosystems that are missing. Do not duplicate or override existing entries. If an existing entry uses the wrong ecosystem (e.g., `pip` when the project uses `uv`), update it to the correct one.

6. **Use `version: 2`** at the top of the file.

7. **If no ecosystems are detected** (no package manager files, no Dockerfiles, no GitHub Actions workflows), do NOT create a `dependabot.yml`. Instead, close this issue with a comment explaining that the repository was analyzed and no supported dependency ecosystems were found. Use a friendly tone, e.g.:
   > 👋 I took a good look around and this repo doesn't appear to have any package managers, Docker files, or GitHub Actions workflows that Dependabot can monitor. No configuration needed — closing this one out! If dependencies are added later, feel free to reopen this issue.

### Example for a repo with npm + Docker + GitHub Actions

```yaml
version: 2
updates:
  - package-ecosystem: "npm"
    directory: "/"
    schedule:
      interval: "weekly"
      day: "monday"
    groups:
      production-dependencies:
        dependency-type: "production"
      development-dependencies:
        dependency-type: "development"
    open-pull-requests-limit: 10

  - package-ecosystem: "docker"
    directory: "/"
    schedule:
      interval: "weekly"
      day: "monday"
    groups:
      docker-updates:
        patterns: ["*"]
    open-pull-requests-limit: 10

  - package-ecosystem: "github-actions"
    directory: "/"
    schedule:
      interval: "weekly"
      day: "monday"
    groups:
      actions-updates:
        patterns: ["*"]
    open-pull-requests-limit: 10
```

---

Thanks for keeping the codebase healthy! 💚
If anything looks off in the PR, just leave a comment and we'll sort it out.

— Your friendly neighbourhood Platform Team 🕸️

items.title: Spring UserReport [2025.06.21] Externally launched spring crashed with code 0
Move the cloudflared containers from iac/server to iac/app
items.body:
The `cloudflared` tunnel containers (one per environment) are managed by `iac/server`, which is the only reason that module needs the docker provider. Because of that, `tofu plan`/`apply` in `iac/server` need SSH access to the server, and a from-scratch build needs `tofu apply -target=hcloud_server.doedensonline` before a full apply. Moving the containers into `iac/app` lets each environment's deploy manage its own tunnel and removes Docker from `iac/server` entirely.

## Design

- **Tunnel token via GitHub Actions secrets.** `iac/server` adds `DEV_TUNNEL_TOKEN` / `PROD_TUNNEL_TOKEN` to `github_actions_{dev,prod}_secrets` from the existing `cloudflare_zero_trust_tunnel_cloudflared_token` data sources, like the other `DEV_*`/`PROD_*` deploy settings. `terraform_remote_state` would give CI access to the infra state (which `DeployState` doesn't allow), and a Cloudflare provider in `iac/app` would put a Cloudflare API token in CI.
- **One container per workspace.** The `for_each = ["dev", "prod"]` goes away; each `iac/app` workspace manages a single tunnel container with the existing `local.log_opts`.
- **New name, run side by side.** The new container is named `${local.name}-tunnel` (`doedensonline-<env>-tunnel`) and runs as a second connector (replica) on the same tunnel next to the old `-cloudflared` container until that one is removed. No cross-state import, no downtime, and the server apply and prod release can happen in either order. Keeping the `-cloudflared` name instead costs a short outage per environment (remove the old container right before that environment's deploy).
- **Pinned image tag.** `iac/app` pins `cloudflare/cloudflared:2026.10.0` (the current `latest`) instead of following `latest` through `docker_registry_image` and `pull_triggers`. Tunnel updates then become reviewed commits: a bump reaches dev on merge and prod with the next release, like the app itself. Dependabot's `opentofu` ecosystem only bumps providers and modules, not image tags in `.tf` files, so the tag is bumped by hand.
- **`keep_locally = true` on every `cloudflared` image resource.** The dev and prod workspaces each manage a `docker_image` for `cloudflared` on the same host. When a tag bump reaches dev before prod, dev's replacement runs `docker rmi` on the old image, which prod's container still uses, and the apply fails. The flag prevents that. The same flag on the server's `docker_image.cloudflared` lets it be deleted later without removing the image the new containers use. Tested with provider 4.6.0: flipping `keep_locally` to `true` is an in-place update (no image replacement, no tunnel restart), and destroying the resource afterwards keeps the image.

## Plan

### PR 1: add the tunnel to `iac/app` ✅ #270

- `iac/server/main.tf`: add `DEV_TUNNEL_TOKEN` / `PROD_TUNNEL_TOKEN` to the secrets locals and `keep_locally = true` to `docker_image.cloudflared`. Apply by hand **before merging**, so the secrets exist for the first deploy that needs them.
- `iac/app/main.tf`:
  - `variable "tunnel_token"`: `sensitive = true`, with a validation that it isn't empty (a missing secret reaches tofu as `TF_VAR_tunnel_token=""`, which would start a crash-looping container).
  - `docker_image.cloudflared` with name `cloudflare/cloudflared:2026.10.0` and `keep_locally = true`. No `docker_registry_image` data source or `pull_triggers`.
  - `docker_container.cloudflared`: name `"${local.name}-tunnel"`, `network_mode = "host"`, `restart = "always"`, the same `command`, `env = ["TUNNEL_TOKEN=${var.tunnel_token}"]`, json-file logging with `local.log_opts`.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: add `TF_VAR_tunnel_token: ${{ secrets[format('{0}_TUNNEL_TOKEN', env.SECRETS)] }}` to the deploy step.
- `.github/dependabot.yml`: add `cloudflared` to the "Not covered on purpose" comment (Dependabot can't bump image tags in `.tf` files, so it's bumped by hand).
- README "Deploy manually": add `-var tunnel_token=...`.
- Rollout: the merge deploys the dev replica, the next release the prod replica. Check that each tunnel shows two connectors in the Cloudflare dashboard (or `docker ps` on the host).

### PR 2: remove Docker from `iac/server` (after both replicas are up) ✅ #271

- Commit 1: delete `docker_container.cloudflared`, `docker_image.cloudflared`, `data.docker_registry_image.cloudflared` and the `tunnel_tokens` local. Apply by hand: this destroys the old containers and leaves the image in place.
- Commit 2: delete `provider "docker"`, the `docker` entry in `required_providers` and the `docker_log_opts` local, and run `tofu init` to prune it from `.terraform.lock.hcl`. This changes no state, so it needs no apply. (It has to come after the apply: destroying the containers needs the provider.)
- After the apply: run `docker rmi cloudflare/cloudflared:latest` on the host. The image stays behind because of `keep_locally`; if it's the same image as the pinned tag, this only removes the `latest` tag.
- Docs:
  - CLAUDE.md: drop the "everything else on the host runs as Docker containers … need SSH access" bullet and the "keep the two `log_opts` copies in sync" note; list the tunnels under `iac/app`.
  - README "Setup infrastructure": drop the SSH / `-target` paragraph; note that the tunnels come up with each environment's first deploy.

## Side effects

- New `cloudflared` releases no longer arrive on their own and nothing flags them: the tag is bumped by hand. The deploy that rolls out a bump restarts the tunnel, but it replaces the app container anyway, so this adds no new downtime.
- A freshly provisioned server has no tunnel until each environment's first deploy.
- The ingress ports (`localhost:8080` / `8081`) stay in the server's `cloudflare_zero_trust_tunnel_cloudflared_config`, while `iac/app` owns the port mapping, so they still have to match by hand. Moving the tunnel config too would need Cloudflare credentials in CI (out of scope).
