items.body:
## Production reconciliation — 2026-10-11

**Delivered migration and independent deployment; open for remaining acceptance.** On 2026-10-11 the infrastructure-owned shared Nginx gateway was cut over and production-reconciled to `6819c1c47b14e00a023d8a86aa30cb00bfa9b5a7`; Notoli `env-prod`/running release `05835a38b3ff0aafd6d89c060055a1ffa7d251d5` includes #906, #908, and #907. Independent initial+repeat Actions deployments succeeded, including immutable images, app-only activation/locks, healthy release records, database snapshot/isolated restoration, recovery retention, and no impact to MacroMapper or ingress. Public/origin/API/OAuth discovery and MCP challenge probes plus an existing authenticated read-only connector operation passed. Cloudflare's configuration did not change; the release client uses `JudeAppRelease/1.0`. Targeted cleanup reclaimed 203.68 MiB. [Production matrix](https://github.com/VanillaIceCube/JudeAndrewAlabaInfrastructure/issues/4#issuecomment-6113551888) · [final source activation](https://github.com/VanillaIceCube/JudeAndrewAlabaInfrastructure/issues/4#issuecomment-6114144231).

**Outstanding / not claimed:** fresh sign-in/registration/consent and mutating feature tests; port 3000 disposition (its original binding intentionally remains); live rollback, host reboot, recurring off-VM backups, and monitoring/alerts. Keep this issue open and Project status **In Progress**. Do not treat a successful isolated restore as a live rollback or reboot test.

---

## ⛔ HARD STOP — NO MERGING WITHOUT EXPLICIT OWNER AUTHORIZATION

**This directive applies to ALL three agents (Notoli, MacroMapper, and VM), any helper/sub-agent, automation, and all PRs related to these tickets. The owner has NOT granted blanket permission to merge.**

- **NEVER merge a pull request into `main`, `env-prod`, or any other branch without the owner's explicit, PR-specific approval given after reviewing that PR.** The instruction to implement a ticket, make a PR, fix review comments, or continue working is **not** merge authorization.
- **NEVER enable auto-merge**, queue a merge, configure bots to merge, or circumvent branch protections. Do not ask other agents/bots to merge on your behalf.
- A **green CI run, bot or human review approval, resolved comments, passing tests, agreement among agents, or “ready for review” state does NOT constitute the owner's authorization to merge.** Neither does silence or previously merged PR #239, which was merged without the owner's authorization.
- **Never push directly to a protected/release branch** (especially `env-prod`) or trigger a workflow that deploys, unless the owner separately authorizes that specific action. Do not treat merge approval as deployment authorization.
- Allowed: investigate, make changes on feature branches, test, create/update reviewable PRs, answer review comments, and post an `[AWAITING OWNER MERGE APPROVAL]` handoff with PR links, changed files, test evidence, risks, and rollback guidance.
- **STOP at the review/approval checkpoint.** If the owner has not explicitly approved the exact PR merge, leave it open and unmerged. If unsure whether approval applies, ask before proceeding.
- **Separate approvals required:** (1) architecture contract; (2) each PR merge; (3) each production deployment/cutover. Approval for one never implies approval for another.

## ⚠️ Owner clarification — PR #239 was merged without authorization

**The owner reports that [MacroMapper PR #239](https://github.com/VanillaIceCube/MacroMapper/pull/239) was merged by Codex without the owner's explicit approval or authorization.** The fact that its commits now exist on `main` **does not mean the owner reviewed, approved, or endorsed its implementation or architecture**.

**Mandatory instructions for this coordinated deployment plan:**
- Treat the PR #239 changes on `main` as **unreviewed candidate implementation**, not as an accepted design, complete deployment prerequisite, or source of truth for what the owner wants.
- **Audit the diff and the actual running Notoli/host configuration independently** before reusing any part of PR #239; identify essential shared-ingress/security/data-preservation changes, unnecessary scaffolding, duplicate documentation/tests, and possible cross-application coupling.
- Compare proposed components against the existing, working Notoli deployment and the agreed long-term goal: **VM-owned shared infrastructure, independently deployable applications, consistent conventions, minimal justified complexity**.
- Explicitly recommend **keep, simplify, replace, or revert** for major PR #239 components. Do not assume that because it is merged it must remain.
- **Do not merge further PRs, change live deployment infrastructure, or deploy the PR #239 implementation without explicit owner approval of the plan and intended changes.** Keep any corrective changes isolated and reviewable; preserve working services and a rollback path.
- Cross-reference the companion issue so both agents/repositories follow this instruction. If earlier wording in this ticket calls PR #239 a merged baseline, that is a statement of Git history **only**, not approval of its contents.

## Three-agent coordination — VM auditor and production operator

**This project has THREE agents, not two.** The two repository agents may investigate and prepare PRs in parallel. A third agent has shell access **on the existing DigitalOcean VM** and is the authoritative observer of *live host state*. The single shared discussion/decision thread remains **[Notoli #904](https://github.com/VanillaIceCube/Notoli/issues/904)**; [MacroMapper #240](https://github.com/VanillaIceCube/MacroMapper/issues/240) tracks the app implementation. This section supplements the two-repository protocol below and takes precedence wherever the old wording assumes only two agents.

### Role separation and source of truth
| Participant | Owns | May do immediately | Must NOT do without specific owner approval |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Agent 1 — Notoli** | Shared architecture *coordination*, Notoli-specific repository changes, proposed migration of shared ingress out of Notoli | Audit repo, draft shared contract, answer questions, prepare reviewable app-local PR | Merge PRs, edit live host, claim VM facts without VM audit |
| **Agent 2 — MacroMapper** | Critically audit unauthorized PR #239; simplify and align MacroMapper-specific code | Audit repo/PR, propose keep/simplify/replace/revert, review contract, prepare independent PR | Merge PRs, edit Notoli or live shared host, implement unapproved shared assumptions |
| **Agent 3 — VM** | Live-environment verification; later, **sole designated production operator** | **Read-only** commands to inspect actual services/configuration/resource usage; publish sanitized findings | Change files, install packages, create Docker networks/containers, restart/reload services, edit DNS/firewalls, take disruptive backups, merge or deploy |

**GitHub repository state is not proof of runtime deployment**; **the VM's state is not a substitute for reviewed source code**. All three must reconcile discrepancies before agreeing on a contract. The owner is the sole authority for approval.

### Immediate VM audit — required BEFORE architecture approval
VM agent: conduct an **inspection-only** audit and post a comment on **Notoli #904** headed `[VM AUDIT]`. If you cannot comment from the VM session, provide a sanitized Markdown report for the owner to post on #904. Record observations and evidence with commands used/time checked where possible, but **never post passwords, environment file contents, API tokens, private keys, full certificate PEMs, or any sensitive Docker inspect `Env` values**. Include:

- Running/stopped containers, Compose project/service labels, image tags/digests, actual mounts **by safe path only**, restart policies, exposed and bound host ports; note whether MacroMapper is deployed at all.
- Active Nginx owner, effective virtual host/routing configuration (redacted as necessary), the Notoli and MacroMapper hostname behavior, TLS certificate coverage/expiration **metadata only**, and Cloudflare/origin discrepancies if observable.
- Docker networks, subnets and members, particularly Notoli's proxy/backend trusted peer `172.30.88.2` / `172.30.88.3`, any `macromapper-ingress` network and whether the proxy is attached; preserve the current MCP/OAuth forwarding trust model.
- RAM, CPU, swap, disk/headroom; identify constraints for adding another app (historical host size ~2 GiB, **do not assume current usage or adequate capacity**).
- Persistent database/volume locations and file ownership/permissions **without opening database contents**, existing backup locations/retention and restore evidence if any; deployed GHCR/SSH/CI capability **as presence or absence, not secret values**.
- Differences between live reality, Notoli's `main`/`env-prod` deployment configuration, and MacroMapper's merged-but-unapproved PR #239; classify facts as **observed**, **repository-only**, or **unknown**. Call out known availability/security risks and safe rollback prerequisites.

**Read-only means no `docker compose up/down/pull`, `docker restart`, `nginx -s reload`, network creation, file edits, migration, package installation, GitHub workflow dispatch, destructive cleanup, or production cutover.** Do not execute a production test with side effects. If an audit step would expose a secret or change state, skip it and document the blocker.

### Required review and decision sequence
1. **Parallel discovery:** Notoli and MacroMapper agents audit their own repositories. VM agent posts `[VM AUDIT]` on Notoli #904. Both repository agents must explicitly read the audit.
2. **Reconcile host facts:** Notoli agent posts `[VM RECONCILIATION]` on #904, mapping VM observations to proposed shared ingress, Notoli proxy trust/security constraints, resources, existing deployment scripts, and rollback plan. MacroMapper agent verifies the mapped upstreams and calls out `[ARCH QUESTION]` conflicts on the same ticket.
3. **Architecture contract:** Notoli agent publishes `[ARCH CONTRACT — PROPOSED]` on #904. MacroMapper agent posts `[CONTRACT REVIEW]`; VM agent posts `[VM FEASIBILITY REVIEW]` for host-specific viability, migration, permissions and capacity. **No owner approval may be requested as “ready” until the VM audit and these reviews are incorporated or unresolved risks are explicitly presented.**
4. **Human approval gate:** Only after the owner explicitly approves the contract may the repository agents finalize changes dependent on it. They may still prepare reversible, app-local PRs before approval. Agents do not auto-approve one another's decisions.
5. **Separate code and production gates:** Repository agents submit scoped PRs with `[IMPLEMENTATION HANDOFF]` on their tickets. **Do not merge without explicit owner authorization.** Once approved code is merged and a separate **explicit production authorization** is given, the VM agent is the **single production change operator**. No other agent simultaneously touches production.
6. **Sequential release:** VM agent publishes `[DEPLOYMENT PLAN — OWNER APPROVAL REQUIRED]` with commands/actions, expected effects, downtime/risks, prereq backups and verified rollback; await explicit approval. Execute ingress/Notoli cutover first, record `[DEPLOYMENT RESULT]` with evidence and verify Notoli + MCP/OAuth; only then deploy MacroMapper, verify both, and check repeat independent deploys. Stop and escalate on discrepancies or failed acceptance, using approved rollback procedures.
7. **Closeout:** VM agent provides `[PRODUCTION HANDOFF]` containing deployed image SHAs, topology, redacted checks/results, backup/restore verification, remaining limitations and operating runbook; repository agents reconcile docs and cross-link results before requesting ticket closure. **A successful CI run is not proof of production launch.**

### Async communication and conflict handling
GitHub issue comments are **not a real-time messaging bus** and do not automatically wake suspended Codex agents. Re-read the Notoli #904 comments at assigned milestones or resume agents manually. All cross-repository and VM questions belong on #904; leave links on #240 rather than branching the discussion. If the VM cannot post directly, the owner relays its sanitized report. **Never infer consent from a comment, silence, bot approval, or the prior unauthorized PR #239 merge.**

**Notoli agent-specific responsibility:** Request the `[VM AUDIT]` report before locking shared ingress/network assumptions; obtain the `[VM FEASIBILITY REVIEW]` before requesting architecture approval. Coordinate with the VM agent, but **do not delegate silent production changes**. Preserve known Notoli MCP/OAuth trust and test it during the cutover.

## Agent-to-agent coordination protocol (required before shared changes)

**These two GitHub tickets are the entire coordination brief for all three agents.** The two repository implementation agents may work in parallel, but must use **[Notoli #904](https://github.com/VanillaIceCube/Notoli/issues/904) as the single shared-architecture discussion and decision thread**. Use [MacroMapper #240](https://github.com/VanillaIceCube/MacroMapper/issues/240) for MacroMapper-specific work. Do not rely on private agent chats, verbal assumptions, or inferred consent.

### Shared communication rules
1. **Read both issue bodies and the latest comments** before beginning; review them again before committing to a cross-application interface, before opening a final PR, and whenever the other agent links a new decision. GitHub comments are **asynchronous** and do **not** reliably wake or notify the other running agent. A posted comment is not an answer or an approval.
2. Keep shared decisions on **Notoli #904 only**. For each blocker/question, leave a structured comment headed `[ARCH QUESTION]` explaining (a) the specific question or conflict, (b) relevant repository paths/runtime constraints, (c) options with tradeoffs, (d) recommended resolution, (e) which agent is expected to respond. Then link that comment in your own issue if applicable.
3. Respond in the **same #904 thread** with `[ARCH RESPONSE]`, including evidence or a concrete counterproposal. Do not spawn duplicate conversations across both issue threads.
4. The infrastructure coordinator must consolidate the decisions into **one explicit versioned architecture contract**, posted on #904 with status `PROPOSED — OWNER APPROVAL REQUIRED`. At minimum specify: infra ownership/source-of-truth location, canonical ingress network and Docker naming, per-app network boundaries and accepted proxy headers/trust, FQDN/vhost routes (including Notoli MCP/OAuth), TLS/cert handling, app-specific release/rollback interface, secret boundaries, and non-disruptive migration order. The MacroMapper agent must comment `[CONTRACT REVIEW]` with either compatibility acknowledgment or objections.
5. **Only the human owner's explicit approval** can change contract status to approved or authorize a merge, deployment, new infrastructure repository, or live VM changes. Neither silence, agent agreement, CI green, an existing merged PR, nor a bot approval counts. If a question is unresolved, do not assume a default; record `[BLOCKED — OWNER DECISION]` and continue only with genuinely independent work.
6. Each agent owns changes **only in its assigned repository** and may open its own reviewable PR. Do not modify the other repo, start concurrent SSH/VM actions, recreate shared Nginx, or deploy. Coordinate cross-repo requirements via the contract and tickets.
7. **Parallelism rules:** audits, research, app-local code cleanup and tests can proceed concurrently. Cross-repo interfaces must follow the agreed contract. Production rollout is sequential: shared infrastructure/Notoli cutover → verified Notoli functionality and rollback capability → MacroMapper deployment → both apps' independent redeploy checks.
8. Before handing a PR to the owner, comment `[IMPLEMENTATION HANDOFF]` on your own ticket: what changed, how it matches the contract, evidence/tests, outstanding questions, precise risks/rollback, and cross-ticket links. Do **not** merge your own PR or begin deployment.

### Explicit PR #239 safeguard
The owner states [MacroMapper PR #239](https://github.com/VanillaIceCube/MacroMapper/pull/239) was merged by Codex **without authorization**. Treat the merged code as potentially useful but **not approved**, and explicitly recommend keep/simplify/replace/revert after checking the actual working system. Do not use its presence on `main` as evidence of owner consent.

### Your role: Notoli / shared-infrastructure coordinator
- Act as **coordination lead, not unilateral architect**: perform a read-only host/configuration audit first; propose the minimum common contract in a comment on **this issue (#904)** and request review from the MacroMapper agent on #240.
- In the contract, protect Notoli's current production routing and exact trusted-proxy boundary; identify which infrastructure currently belongs to Notoli and how it can safely become host-owned. Do not presume PR #239's override is permanent.
- Read MacroMapper's `[CONTRACT REVIEW]` response on this issue; address disagreements here, consolidate the revision, and ask the owner for explicit contract approval **before implementing consequential shared-boundary changes**.
- You may separately prepare non-disruptive Notoli-local changes and tests while awaiting review. No live VM modifications or merges without explicit owner approval.

## Objective
Establish a **small, reusable multi-application hosting foundation** on the existing DigitalOcean VM, without making Notoli the permanent owner of MacroMapper's or future apps' ingress. Retain the existing stack—**Cloudflare + one Nginx entrypoint + Docker Compose + GHCR + per-app Django/React/SQLite + GitHub Actions**—and make adding a third app routine.

**This is the host/Notoli half of a coordinated two-repository plan.** The companion MacroMapper issue will implement the application's adoption and first public launch. No code, DNS, container, or production change is authorized by the creation of this issue alone.

### Current evidence / why this is needed
- Notoli currently owns host **80/443** via `notoli-proxy`; its frontend also publishes **3000**.
- Notoli's MCP/ASGI trusted-proxy policy depends on the exact private proxy peer `172.30.88.2` and backend `172.30.88.3` on `notoli_backend_private`. Breaking this can break HTTPS/OAuth or weaken forwarding-header validation. See [Notoli #896](https://github.com/VanillaIceCube/Notoli/issues/896).
- The existing Notoli deploy workflow manages/recreates its proxy and runs host-wide `docker system prune -af`: dangerous for multiple apps.
- MacroMapper's [PR #239 (merged)](https://github.com/VanillaIceCube/MacroMapper/pull/239) introduced a **bridge** using `deploy/notoli.compose.override.yml` and a shared Nginx vhost. It is useful work but should not become the permanent architecture where one app supplies another app's deployment files.
- Existing Droplet documentation indicates ~2 GiB RAM; verify current free memory, disk, CPU and swap **on the live host** before onboarding another app.

## Agreed target architecture / design contract
1. **One public ingress, independent owner.** One Nginx instance owns 80/443 and routes by FQDN (including Notoli `/mcp` and `/.well-known/`). Cloudflare remains DNS/TLS front door. Store canonical, version-controlled **host-owned ingress configuration outside both app deployment projects** (prefer a small separate host-infrastructure repository/directory; discuss repository ownership before creating it). App deployments must never overwrite/recreate this proxy. Do not introduce Traefik/Kubernetes/Terraform without a demonstrated need.
2. **One Compose project per app.** Independent frontend, backend, database file/volume, env/secrets, deployment workflow, logs, health checks and releases. Namespaced service/container/DNS identifiers, avoiding collisions. No app should publish public backend ports; eliminate direct public frontend ports where safe. Use **per-app isolated networks**, attached to the shared ingress only for routes that require it. Do not expose databases or unrelated backend internals to other applications. Per-app backend egress must still work.
3. **Preserve Notoli's security invariant during the cutover.** Either retain trusted private proxy peer `172.30.88.2` and its reserved network address while migrating ingress ownership, or explicitly redesign the trusted-proxy mechanism and prove the equivalent safety before changing the IP. Do not set universal trusted forwarding headers or disable OAuth/MCP protections for convenience.
4. **Standard app deployment contract, not duplicated infrastructure engines.** Both repositories own their own GitHub Actions release pipeline but follow the same conventions: `main` for development, reviewed `env-prod` release, SHA-tagged GHCR images, isolated app-only deployments, secret-managed environment, predictable revision record, serialized release, minimal health check, and safe rollback. A tiny reusable workflow/template can be extracted **after** a proven deployment; avoid a complex common framework first.
5. **Data and operations isolation.** Keep SQLite per app for now; consistent backup before risky migrations and scheduled off-VM backups plus test restores. Explicit permissions, monitoring, disk/resource thresholds, log retention, and a documented restore process. App deployments cannot prune other apps' Docker artifacts, reset their networks, rotate their secrets, or delete their databases.
6. **Scalability boundary.** This standard scales organizationally to more apps on a single VM, **not infinitely in capacity**. Measure CPU/RAM/disk (and peak build usage) before onboarding, set upgrade thresholds, and keep app contracts portable to another VM or managed data service later.

## Implementation phases / checkboxes
### Phase A — Baseline and decisions (no service disruption)
- [x] Inventory live VM containers, listening ports, Compose project labels, volumes, Docker networks/subnets, cert mounts, current Notoli deployment files, SSH/GHCR permissions, and CPU/RAM/disk usage; compare with checked-in configuration.
- [x] Capture recoverable Notoli DB snapshot and current proxy/Compose/image configurations **before** changes; verify recovery commands.
- [x] Document canonical ownership and directory layout for shared ingress and app deployments; choose source of truth (separate host-owned config vs temporary documented host directory) **without silently adding another infrastructure service**.
- [x] Write a concise architecture decision and cutover/rollback runbook; agree on maintenance window and smoke tests.

### Phase B — Establish independent shared ingress
- [x] Version-control host-owned ingress Compose/config and subdomain vhosts; preserve Cloudflare Full (strict) origin TLS and existing certificate access without copying private keys into repos.
- [x] Attach ingress to the **minimum required** per-app frontend/backend networks using unique upstream names and safe runtime DNS behavior when an app is down.
- [x] **Preserve Notoli's exact ASGI proxy-trust boundary** during migration, including static address allocation and backend outbound connectivity; explicitly test the bridge and reject arbitrary forwarded headers.
- [x] Move Notoli's public proxy lifecycle out of Notoli's app-deployment workflow via a staged, reversible cutover. Ensure old proxy cannot restart and contend for 80/443; do not run conflicting proxies simultaneously.
- [x] Keep Notoli available throughout preparation and plan/record any short cutover window. Verify old Nginx can be restored promptly if new routing fails.

### Phase C — Normalize Notoli's app deployment
- [x] Keep Notoli as its own Compose project, with app-scoped deploy `up`/migration/restart only; **no host-wide `docker system prune -af`, no cross-project `down`, no implicit shared-proxy restart**.
- [ ] Preserve routes `/`, `/auth/`, `/api/`, `/admin/`, `/mcp`, `/.well-known/`, static files, websocket/streaming requirements and OAuth discovery/challenges; ensure no auth caching.
- [ ] Remove or loopback-bind direct public port 3000 if not needed, without breaking any known consumer; backend remains private.
- [x] Align release naming, SHA-selection, health checks, backup-before-migration, recovery procedures, and release docs with the MacroMapper adoption ticket.
- [ ] Check repeat deployments, rollback, VM reboot, and app restarts do not affect another application or the ingress.

### Phase D — App onboarding standard and operations
- [ ] Publish a short **new-app checklist/template**: domain/DNS/TLS, app-specific Compose project/network, safe route inclusion, secrets, GHCR/tag, database path, CI/CD, healthcheck, smoke tests, rollback and cleanup.
- [ ] Define ownership and operational runbooks: ingress changes isolated from app releases; secret rotation; TLS renewal/expiry; Cloudflare cache bypass; off-VM backups and restore drills; basic availability and resource alerts.
- [x] Verify host capacity for 2 apps; document resource upgrade decision for a third and the eventual multi-VM boundary.
- [ ] Cross-check and close only after MacroMapper's companion ticket proves independent production deployment.

## Required verification / acceptance
- [ ] Notoli works **before and after** proxy cutover: frontend, sign-in, API, `/mcp` / `/.well-known/` OAuth discovery and actual connected plugin actions (where credentials available).
- [ ] Ingress remains reachable if either app is down and restarting/redeploying Notoli does not stop or mutate MacroMapper.
- [x] Ingress is **not owned/deployed by Notoli or MacroMapper**; the shared vhost/network changes are versioned with a documented owner.
- [x] Both apps ultimately follow compatible release, rollback, secrets, backup and logging conventions with isolated DBs/networks.
- [x] No public backend listener, destructive shared-host cleanup, credential leakage or proxy-trust regression.
- [ ] Restore/rollback has been practiced, and actual production evidence (not just local CI) is recorded in both tickets.

## Non-goals
No product changes, forced migration from SQLite, shared Django process/database, Kubernetes, automatic horizontal autoscaling, new paid infrastructure services, wholesale auth changes or extra refactoring for aesthetics. **Preserve existing Notoli production first.**

## References
- [MacroMapper #236 — broad launch acceptance](https://github.com/VanillaIceCube/MacroMapper/issues/236)
- [MacroMapper #238 — minimum launch prerequisites](https://github.com/VanillaIceCube/MacroMapper/issues/238)
- [MacroMapper PR #239 — merged bridge to preserve/trim](https://github.com/VanillaIceCube/MacroMapper/pull/239)

items.title: mise migration: cutover runbook and lessons learned for CachyOS and macOS
items.body:
The Omarchy laptop has been cut over to the `mise-migration` branch and passes every check. This issue is the handoff for the **CachyOS desktop** and the **MacBook**. An agent running on one of those machines should read this issue and `AGENTS.md` on the branch, then work through the cutover for that machine only. The laptop's session, plan file and scripts are not available there, so everything needed is below. **Branch state** (`origin/mise-migration`): | Commit | Change | | --- | --- | | `2bf6e53` | Replace Ansible with mise modules | | `a36e56d`, `46b0f6e` | Omarchy: reload Hyprland from any shell, ignore stale signatures | | `4daaf87` | Allow the reviewed `svelte@4.2.20` past mise's npm trust policy | | `a869932` | Declare `node = "lts"` only for CachyOS and macOS (Omarchy pins node itself) | | `bfdcbd4` | jj's email follows 1Password, like git's | | `133b8fa` | Link read-only configs instead of copying them | | `82c74b9` | omp tests: parse check without type packages (bun 1.4.3) | ## Decisions already made (do not relitigate) - The 24 dropped roles stay dropped: awesomewm, vicinae, nala, flatpak, alacritty, fabric, docker, pwsh, ruby, rust, kind, just, aws, orbstack, wireguard, glab, yazi, sesh, azure, goreleaser, kwctl, nomad, tshark, github_release. None of them ran on a plain `dotfiles` on any machine. **But** check whether yazi, sesh, glab or pwsh config is in use on this machine before the stale-link step, and report it: links into the old `roles/` tree get deleted there. - `~/.claude/settings.json` stays a symlink. `~/.claude/{commands,agents,hooks,scripts}` stay whole-directory links. - No `DisableDownloadTimeout` in `/etc/pacman.conf`. - Full system upgrades stay out of `dotfiles`; the `update` alias does them. - Ask the owner before any `git push`. The owner opens the PR once all three machines pass. ## Lessons learned on the laptop 1. **Isolate every test run from the live config.** `bin/dotfiles` and mise honour `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`. A test that only changed `HOME` still wrote `~/.config/mise/conf.d` and `miserc.local.toml` on the real machine. For experiments, point `HOME`, every `XDG_*`, and `MISE_CONFIG_DIR`, `MISE_STATE_DIR`, `MISE_DATA_DIR`, `MISE_CACHE_DIR`, `MISE_SYSTEM_CONFIG_DIR` into a temp dir. The preflight script below is safe: it only swaps the config and state dirs and never applies anything. 2. **`mise run` installs tools.** By default it installs every missing `[tools]` entry before running a task. Set `MISE_TASK_RUN_AUTO_INSTALL=false` (and `MISE_AUTO_INSTALL`, `MISE_EXEC_AUTO_INSTALL`, `MISE_NOT_FOUND_AUTO_INSTALL`) for sandbox or test runs. `mise bootstrap --dry-run` never runs module tasks; it only prints `mise run --jobs 1 'bootstrap:*'`. 3. **A failed tool install stops the run before any module task.** The tools step runs before `bootstrap:*`. On the laptop, gopls timed out on proxy.golang.org (transient; `mise install go:golang.org/x/tools/gopls` worked on retry) and svelte-language-server hit mise's npm trust policy (fixed on the branch). Until that was fixed, the secrets, omp, system and other tasks never ran. For a new trust-downgrade error: check the npm publisher and that an upstream git tag exists, then add the narrowest `trust_policy_excludes = ["pkg@version"]`. Never use `npm.shell_out`. 4. **Conflicts are expected; force only once the checker explains every difference.** mise will not replace a real file with a link (`refusing to overwrite existing files`), and the whole run stops at the dotfiles step. The branch now links many files Ansible copied, so expect many conflicts: - **Every machine:** zsh files, ghostty, kitty, lsd, lfk, gh-dash, worktrunk, `~/Taskfile.yml` (Linux), `commit_template`, omp `AGENTS.md`. - **CachyOS and Mac:** `tmux.conf`, neofetch, the btop theme. - **Mac only:** `~/.bashrc`, `~/.profile`, `~/.config/bash`, starship, bat, the four k9s files, `bordersrc`. If the checker reports `same bytes`, forcing is lossless. `DIFFERENT bytes` is fine only for the files the port itself edited (the list under 6a). Anything else is local drift: copy the live content into the module source and commit it in the worktree before forcing, or move the live file to `.pre-mise`. 5. **mise bug: never force over a directory link where per-file links go.** If a target is a whole-directory symlink and its entry is `mode = "symlink-each"`, `--force-dotfiles` writes links *through* the old link into the source tree, replacing the source files with links to themselves. The checker prints `DIR-LINK` for this case; delete that directory link first. Ansible used per-file links or copies for every per-file target, so none are expected, but check. 6. **Copies overwrite live edits silently.** The remaining copies (fcitx5 `keyboard.conf`, `btop.conf`, `karabiner.json`, codex agents, Claude `skill-creator`, `~/.hammerspoon`, 1Password `agent.toml`) are rewritten on every run. The checker's `CONTENT-DIFF` lines are the only warning. Save live edits with `mise dot add ` first, or edit the module source. 7. **Don't edit `~/.dotfiles` before the cutover.** On `main` it still backs live symlinks. Work in the worktree and commit fixes there. 8. **Run the cutover (6b) from a plain terminal**, not inside omp or herdr. Between checkout and relink, the omp, cursor and Claude configs point at deleted files. After step 5 relinks everything, the rest can run from anywhere. 9. **A module folder's own `mise.toml` is project config while you are inside it.** Its `[tools]` override global pins there and during that module's `bootstrap:` task. That is why `node` is declared only in `modules/devtools/mise.cachyos.toml` and `mise.macos.toml`. 10. **Normal dry-run noise:** - `edit ~/.config/jj/config.toml (merge:shared) (if changed)` always appears, because dry-runs don't render templates. - `permissions not set` warnings appear for files a merge will create. - On CachyOS, the keyd service warns until keyd is installed. 11. **A fresh setup needs `dotfiles` twice.** Permission entries for files that merges create apply on the second run. 12. **1Password.** `bootstrap:secrets` waits up to 20 s for `op` when 1Password is locked, then continues with the last synced values. It may pop a 1Password approval prompt. macOS has no GNU `timeout`, so the script bounds `op` with perl's `alarm`. 13. **sudo.** Dry-runs read `/etc` through sudo. Until the `/etc/sudoers.d` file is deployed, expect password prompts. 14. **`bin/dotfiles` pull rules.** It runs `git pull --ff-only` only when there are no tracked local changes and the branch has an upstream; otherwise it says why. It applies the working tree either way. 15. **Harmless Ansible leftovers** you can delete afterwards: `~/.nvm`, `~/.dotfiles_run`, `~/.config/nvim.backup-*`, kitty `~` backups. ## Runbook `WT=~/.worktrees/.dotfiles/mise-migration`. Profile is `cachyos` or `macos` (`~/.dotfiles/bin/dotfiles --profile` prints it once the branch is checked out in the worktree). ### 0. Prerequisites ```bash git -C ~/.dotfiles fetch origin mise-migration git -C ~/.dotfiles worktree add ~/.worktrees/.dotfiles/mise-migration mise-migration mise --version # must be >= 2026.10.6; if older run `update` (CachyOS) or `brew upgrade mise` (Mac) ``` ### 6a. Preflight (changes nothing live) Save the two scripts at the bottom of this issue as `/tmp/preflight.sh` and `/tmp/check.py`, then: ```bash bash /tmp/preflight.sh cachyos # or: macos python3 /tmp/check.py /tmp/dotfiles-preflight/status.json less /tmp/dotfiles-preflight/dry-run-full.txt /tmp/dotfiles-preflight/packages.txt /tmp/dotfiles-preflight/diff.txt ``` How to read the checker output: | Result | Meaning | Action | | --- | --- | --- | | `MISSING` | First deploy (e.g. Claude and codex were tag-only before) | none | | `TYPE-CONFLICT … same bytes` | Ansible copy where a link now goes | `--force-dotfiles` in step 5 | | `TYPE-CONFLICT … DIFFERENT bytes` | An Ansible copy whose content differs: an expected port edit (list below) or local drift | Port edit: force in step 5. Drift: fold into the module source and commit, or move the live file aside | | `CONTENT-DIFF` | A link or copy whose content differs from the new source | Same rule: expected only for the port edits below | | `OK-RELINK`, `DANGLING` | Link will be repointed | none | | `DIR-LINK` | mise bug hazard (lesson 5) | Delete the directory link before step 5 | | `WOULD-REMOVE` | Retired file (`mode = "absent"`) | none | | `EDIT-MISSING`, `EDIT-DIFFERS` | Block, merge or line edit still to apply (git include block, herdr and other merges, `~/.npmrc` lines) | none: merges add the repo's keys and keep the rest | Expected differences from edits the port made. They show as `CONTENT-DIFF`, or as `TYPE-CONFLICT … DIFFERENT bytes` where Ansible had copied the file: - **zsh:** `claude_functions.zsh` (repo paths) and `paths_vars.zsh` (the mise shims line). - **Taskfile (Linux):** the Ansible header is gone and `dotfiles --check` is now `mise bootstrap --dry-run`. - **Path fixes:** two omp `herdr-workflow` reference docs, and codex `github-issue-hierarchy/SKILL.md`. - **Claude:** `settings.json` gains the `theme`/`tui` keys. - **Mac `bashrc`:** the nvm lines are removed. **CachyOS packages:** if an `aur:` entry is `missing` in `packages.txt` while `pacman -Q ` succeeds, change it to `pacman:` in that module's `mise.cachyos.toml`, commit, and rerun 6a. mise checks `pacman -Qm`, so a repo-installed package never satisfies `aur:`. **Mac packages:** if the dry-run rejects a tap formula (`hashicorp/tap/terraform`, `oven-sh/bun/bun`, `janosmiko/tap/lfk`, `FelixKratz/formulae/borders`), move it into a `BREW_FALLBACK` array in a new `modules/packages/brew-fallback.sh`, run from a `bootstrap:packages` task in `mise.macos.toml` that `brew install`s missing entries. Whether mise's brew manager adds taps on its own was not verifiable from Linux. Also record `ls -l ~/.claude/settings.json` before cutover (is it still a symlink after months of Claude use?). ### 6b. Cutover (plain terminal) ```bash WT=~/.worktrees/.dotfiles/mise-migration # 1. Commit everything in the worktree (status must be empty), then remove it; the branch stays. git -C "$WT" status --short git -C ~/.dotfiles worktree remove "$WT" # 2. Fold ~/.gitconfig into ~/.config/git/config so the mise include block is the last word. if [ -f ~/.gitconfig ] && [ ! -L ~/.gitconfig ]; then mkdir -p ~/.config/git && cat ~/.gitconfig >> ~/.config/git/config && mv ~/.gitconfig ~/.gitconfig.pre-mise fi # Move aside any DIFFERENT-bytes conflict you chose not to fold in: mv .pre-mise # 3. Switch the live checkout (git stash first if it refuses because of local edits). git -C ~/.dotfiles checkout mise-migration # 4. Move ignored state out of the old tree, then delete it. git -C ~/.dotfiles status --ignored --porcelain=v1 roles [ -f ~/.dotfiles/roles/neovim/files/lazy-lock.json ] && mv ~/.dotfiles/roles/neovim/files/lazy-lock.json ~/.dotfiles/modules/neovim/nvim/ ( cd ~/.dotfiles/roles/claude/files 2>/dev/null && find . -mindepth 1 \( -type f -o -type l \) -print ) | while IFS= read -r rel; do rel=${rel#./} mkdir -p ~/.dotfiles/modules/claude/"$(dirname "$rel")" mv ~/.dotfiles/roles/claude/files/"$rel" ~/.dotfiles/modules/claude/"$rel"; done rm -rf ~/.dotfiles/roles # 5. Relink. Without --force it stops on every conflict, which is the expected first result. ~/.dotfiles/bin/dotfiles --only dotfiles || true # Only when every remaining conflict was "same bytes" (or resolved) and there were no DIR-LINK lines: ~/.dotfiles/bin/dotfiles --only dotfiles --force-dotfiles # This is also the recovery command whenever a later step fails: after it, every config is live again. # 6. Full run. If the tools step fails, fix it (lesson 3) and rerun; configs stay linked from step 5. ~/.dotfiles/bin/dotfiles ``` 7. Remove superseded installs, then run `~/.dotfiles/bin/dotfiles` again. It must exit 0 and change nothing. **CachyOS** ```bash sudo rm -f /usr/local/bin/herdr /usr/local/bin/lfk for b in task gopls helm-ls; do for d in ~/.local/bin ~/go/bin; do [ -f "$d/$b" ] && ! grep -qa 'exec mise x' "$d/$b" && rm -f "$d/$b"; done; done [ -f ~/.local/bin/codex ] && ! grep -qa 'exec mise x' ~/.local/bin/codex && rm -f ~/.local/bin/codex [ -e ~/.bun/bin/omp ] && bun remove -g @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent bun remove -g opencode-ai || true rm -f ~/.codex/agents/.managed-by-dotfiles.json ``` **Mac** ```bash rm -f ~/.local/bin/herdr for b in task gopls helm-ls; do for d in ~/.local/bin ~/go/bin; do [ -f "$d/$b" ] && ! grep -qa 'exec mise x' "$d/$b" && rm -f "$d/$b"; done; done brew uninstall --cask codex || true brew uninstall sst/tap/opencode || true bun remove -g @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent || true rm -f ~/.codex/agents/.managed-by-dotfiles.json ``` 8. Stale links into the deleted tree. This is portable, so it works without GNU `find -lname`. Review the list first; dropped roles show up here if they were ever deployed. ```bash stale() { find ~/.config ~/.local/bin ~/.local/share/kwin ~/.omp ~/.claude ~/.codex ~/.cursor ~/.hammerspoon ~/Documents/Superwhisper -xdev -type l 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r l; do case "$(readlink "$l")" in "$HOME/.dotfiles/roles/"*) echo "$l" ;; esac; done; } stale # review stale | while IFS= read -r l; do rm -f "$l"; done ``` ### Verify ```bash cd ~ mise bootstrap status --missing && mise dot status --missing && echo status-ok ~/.dotfiles/bin/dotfiles --dry-run # only the bootstrap task, plus the jj "(if changed)" line realpath ~/.omp/agent/config.yml # ~/.dotfiles/modules/omp/config.yml git config --get user.name # TechDufus d=$(mktemp -d) && (cd "$d" && git init -q && git commit -q --allow-empty -m t && git verify-commit HEAD) [ "$(jj config get user.email)" = "$(git config --get user.email)" ] && echo jj-email-ok zsh -ic 'whence -p gopls typescript-language-server task' # all under ~/.local/share/mise/ zsh -ic 'type nvm' >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo nvm-gone node --version # current LTS (24.x) mise run check # from ~, so no project task shadows it ls -d ~/.dotfiles/roles 2>/dev/null || echo roles-gone ls -l ~/.claude/settings.json # still a symlink after the cutover? ``` - **CachyOS:** - `systemctl --user is-active plasma-summon.service` and `systemctl is-active keyd` both print `active`. - CapsLock summon works. - `steam-health --runtime --strict` exits 0. - `getcap /usr/bin/gamescope` shows `cap_sys_nice`. - **Mac:** - `brew services list` shows borders and ollama `started`. - `grep -c 'hs.application.find' ~/.hammerspoon/Spoons/WorkspaceManager.spoon/summon.lua` prints `0`. - `/Applications/Raycast Beta.app` exists on macOS ≥ 26. - `git config --get core.pager` prints `delta`. - `~/.config/borders/bordersrc` is an executable link. ### 6c. Rollback ```bash rm -f ~/.config/mise/conf.d ~/.config/mise/miserc.local.toml # restore ~/.config/mise/conf.d.pre-dotfiles.* if one exists # Remove the mise git include blocks (macOS: sed -i '' …) sed -i '/^# >>> mise:dotfiles >>>/,/^# <<< mise:dotfiles <<>> mise:dotfiles-macos >>>/,/^# <<< mise:dotfiles-macos <<pacman (CachyOS) / brew fallbacks (Mac): ~/.claude/settings.json before cutover: symlink or regular file? Dropped-role config found in step 8 (yazi/sesh/glab/pwsh/...): Commits made in the worktree (not pushed without asking): Cutover result + verification results: Open items: ``` ## Scripts
/tmp/preflight.sh (read-only preflight) ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash # Throwaway: plan step 6a preflight. Changes nothing live. usage: preflight.sh set -uo pipefail WT=${WT:-$HOME/.worktrees/.dotfiles/mise-migration} profile=${1:-omarchy} case $profile in omarchy | cachyos) envs="\"$profile\"" ;; macos) envs='' ;; *) exit 2 ;; esac ( P=/tmp/dotfiles-preflight rm -rf "$P" mkdir -p "$P/mise" ln -s "$WT/modules" "$P/mise/conf.d" [ -f ~/.config/mise/config.toml ] && cp ~/.config/mise/config.toml "$P/mise/config.toml" printf 'auto_env = true\nenv = [%s]\n' "$envs" >"$P/mise/miserc.local.toml" export MISE_CONFIG_DIR="$P/mise" MISE_STATE_DIR="$P/state" cd ~ || exit 1 mise bootstrap --dry-run --yes >"$P/dry-run.txt" 2>&1 echo "dry-run exit=$?" mise bootstrap --dry-run --yes --force-dotfiles >"$P/dry-run-full.txt" 2>&1 echo "dry-run (force-dotfiles view) exit=$?" mise bootstrap packages status >"$P/packages.txt" 2>&1 echo "packages exit=$?" mise dot status --json >"$P/status.json" echo "status exit=$?" mise dot diff >"$P/diff.txt" 2>&1 echo "diff exit=$?" ) ``` The first dry-run exits 1 on conflicts; that is expected. `dry-run-full.txt` shows the rest of the run.
/tmp/check.py (classifies every non-applied entry) ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Throwaway 6a preflight checker (never committed). usage: check.py Classifies every non-applied [dotfiles] entry and edit from `mise dot status --json`. """ import json import os import sys from pathlib import Path def expand(p: str) -> Path: return Path(os.path.expanduser(p)) def files_under(root: Path): for dirpath, _dirs, names in os.walk(root, followlinks=True): for name in names: yield (Path(dirpath) / name).relative_to(root) def same_bytes(a: Path, b: Path) -> bool: try: return a.read_bytes() == b.read_bytes() except OSError: return False def out(kind: str, target, detail: str = "") -> None: print(f"{kind:15} {target} {detail}".rstrip()) def link_file(target: Path, src: Path, label) -> None: if not os.path.lexists(target): out("MISSING", label) elif not target.is_symlink(): same = "same bytes" if same_bytes(target, src) else "DIFFERENT bytes" out("TYPE-CONFLICT", label, f"(real file where a link is declared; {same})") elif not target.exists(): out("DANGLING", label, f"-> {os.readlink(target)}") elif same_bytes(target.resolve(), src): out("OK-RELINK", label) else: out("CONTENT-DIFF", label, f"(live {target.resolve()})") def link_dir(target: Path, src: Path, label) -> None: if not os.path.lexists(target): out("MISSING", label) return if not target.is_symlink(): out("TYPE-CONFLICT", label, "(real dir where a link is declared)") return live = target.resolve() bad = [str(r) for r in files_under(src) if not same_bytes(live / r, src / r)] if bad: out("CONTENT-DIFF", label, f"({len(bad)} files differ/missing: {', '.join(bad[:6])})") else: out("OK-RELINK", label) def copy_file(target: Path, src: Path, label) -> None: if not os.path.lexists(target): out("MISSING", label) elif target.is_symlink(): same = "same bytes" if same_bytes(target, src) else "DIFFERENT bytes" out("TYPE-SYMLINK", label, f"(live is a symlink -> {os.readlink(target)}; {same})") elif same_bytes(target, src): out("OK-SAME", label, "(bytes equal; metadata/permissions differ)") else: out("CONTENT-DIFF", label) def copy_dir(target: Path, src: Path, label) -> None: if not os.path.lexists(target): out("MISSING", label) return missing, diff = [], [] for rel in files_under(src): live = target / rel if not os.path.lexists(live): missing.append(str(rel)) elif not same_bytes(live, src / rel): diff.append(str(rel)) if diff: out("CONTENT-DIFF", label, f"(differ: {', '.join(diff[:8])})") if missing: out("NEW-FILES", label, f"(new: {', '.join(missing[:8])})") if not diff and not missing: out("OK-SAME", label, "(all source files equal)") def main() -> int: data = json.loads(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text()) counts: dict[str, int] = {} for entry in data.get("files", []): state, mode, label = entry["state"], entry["mode"], entry["target"] counts[state] = counts.get(state, 0) + 1 if state in ("applied", "tracked"): continue target = expand(entry["target"]) src = Path(entry["origin"]["source"]) if entry["origin"].get("source") else None reason = entry.get("reason", "") if mode == "absent": out("WOULD-REMOVE", label, f"({reason})") elif mode == "permissions": cur = oct(os.stat(target).st_mode & 0o7777) if target.exists() else "absent" out("PERMISSIONS", label, f"(current {cur}, desired {entry.get('permissions')})") elif state == "source_missing" or src is None or not src.exists(): out("SOURCE-MISSING", label, f"({entry.get('source')})") elif mode == "symlink-each": if target.is_symlink(): out("DIR-LINK", label, "(a directory link where per-file links go: remove it before --force-dotfiles, or mise writes links through it into the source)") continue for rel in files_under(src): link_file(target / rel, src / rel, f"{label}/{rel}") elif mode == "symlink": (link_dir if src.is_dir() else link_file)(target, src, label) elif mode == "copy": (copy_dir if src.is_dir() else copy_file)(target, src, label) else: out("UNHANDLED", label, f"(mode {mode}, state {state}, {reason})") for edit in data.get("edits", []): if edit["state"] != "applied": out("EDIT-" + edit["state"].upper(), edit["path"], f"({edit['edit']})") print("states:", json.dumps(counts, sort_keys=True)) return 0 if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main()) ```
